Parents and caregivers should stop using any product from that lot and either discard it or return it to the place of purchase for a refund. Anyone who has symptoms after using it should seek medical attention and contact Pacific Health Sciences at 310-457-1775 or myorder@pacifichealth.com, Monday to Thursday, 9:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Pacific. Other lots are not part of this recall.

title: Colorado Indictment: Fake IDs Used to Drain Home Equity Lines at Seven Banks
description: Prosecutors allege more than $800,000 in losses. Both defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser announced Oct. 6 that a statewide grand jury indicted two people for an alleged bank fraud scheme involving home equity lines of credit. The defendants are Stephanie Laugier, 27, and Thierno Barry, 29. An indictment is a formal accusation, and both are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

According to the indictment, Laugier traveled to banks and credit unions in summer 2025 and used a fake state ID to pose as the real holder of a home equity line. She is accused of withdrawing thousands of dollars in cash or having the bank issue a check to a person in another state or, in one case, to a fraudulent business. Those checks were overnighted out of state. The targeted banks were in Arvada, Denver, Dillon, Littleton, Lone Tree, Longmont and Parker.

The attorney general's office says aggregate losses in Colorado exceeded $800,000, with attempted losses above $300,000. It also says victims' personal information was used to file fraudulent business records with the Colorado Secretary of State without their consent. The charges include racketeering, theft, identity theft, forgery of a government document and money laundering. Laugier is in custody in Louisiana, and Barry is still at large.

The case began when a Coloradan reported fraudulent activity. Homeowners with a home equity line can check their statements often and ask their lender what identity checks it requires for in-branch withdrawals. The release does not give advice for consumers, so those are general steps, not part of the announcement.

title: Connecticut Insurance Department Reports $6.4 Million Recovered for Consumers
description: The department also says its life insurance locator matched more than $35 million in coverage.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Connecticut Insurance Department released its fiscal year 2026 results on Oct. 5. It says it recovered more than $6.4 million for Connecticut consumers through complaint resolution and assistance.

The department also reports that its Life Insurance Policy Locator matched more than $35 million in reported life insurance coverage, meaning policies that family members might not have known about were found for them. It says it generated more than $138.6 million for the state's General Fund, including about $41 million from biennial producer appointment fees and $2.6 million from fines and penalties on regulated entities.

Insurance Commissioner Josh Hershman said the results reflect work from resolving individual consumer issues to holding insurers and licensed professionals accountable. The department is funded mainly through assessments on domestic insurance companies rather than the General Fund.

The figures are the department's own and cover Connecticut only. They show that filing a complaint with a state insurance regulator can lead to recoveries, though results vary by case. If you have a dispute with an insurer in another state, your state insurance department has its own complaint process.

title: Connecticut Flood Victims Can Apply for SBA Disaster Loans by Dec. 1
description: Fairfield, New Haven and Litchfield counties are covered. Economic injury loan applications stay open until July 2, 2027.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Connecticut Gov. Ned Lamont announced Oct. 6 that the U.S. Small Business Administration approved a disaster declaration for Fairfield County and the neighboring New Haven and Litchfield counties after the Sept. 13 flash flooding. Homeowners, renters, businesses and nonprofits there can apply for low-interest SBA disaster loans.

According to the governor's office, homeowners can borrow up to $500,000 to repair a primary residence, and homeowners and renters up to $100,000 to repair or replace personal property. Businesses can borrow up to $2 million for real property, inventory, machinery and equipment. Businesses and nonprofits can apply for Economic Injury Disaster Loans of up to $2 million for working capital until normal operations resume.

The deadline for physical damage loan applications is Dec. 1, 2026, and for economic injury loans it is July 2, 2027. A temporary SBA Disaster Loan Outreach Center opens Oct. 7 at the Margaret E. Morton Government Center, 999 Broad Street in Bridgeport. It is open Monday to Friday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Saturday 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., with shorter hours on Oct. 9, 20 and 21, closed Oct. 12, and expected to close permanently at 4 p.m. on Oct. 21.

These are loans, so they must be repaid. The state's emergency services commissioner said the loans are meant for people with uninsured losses. Check the SBA's own application page for current terms and rates before applying, since the governor's release does not list them.

title: Eden Brothers Recalls Calabrese Broccoli Seeds Over Possible Salmonella
description: Two lots sold online and on Amazon from July 8 to Sept. 28 are covered. The company offers full refunds.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Eden Brothers LLC of Arden, North Carolina, announced on Oct. 7 that it is recalling Calabrese broccoli seeds because its supplier said they may be contaminated with Salmonella. The FDA posted the company's notice the same day. The company says no illnesses have been reported.

The recall covers Eden Brothers lots 1022067 and 1022068, supplier lot W4105, in packet, 1-ounce and 1-pound sizes. The lot number is printed on the packet or bag. The seeds were sold on EdenBrothers.com and Amazon.com from July 8 through Sept. 28, 2026, and shipped nationwide. Eden Brothers stopped selling the lots and is contacting customers directly.

The company tells gardeners not to plant, sprout, eat or share the seeds, and not to use them for microgreens. It says to seal the seeds in a bag and throw them in household trash, not compost, then wash hands and any surfaces or containers that touched them. Anyone who gave the seeds to others should tell them about the recall.

Eden Brothers is offering a full refund through a recall reply form on its site, and a team member will follow up. Questions can go to customer service at 855-440-2929, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern, or service@edenbrothers.com. Salmonella can cause serious illness in young children, older adults and people with weak immune systems, according to the company's notice. The FDA says it does not endorse the product or company.

title: FDIC Publishes List of Banks Examined for Community Reinvestment Act Compliance
description: The Oct. 5 list covers ratings the FDIC assigned in July 2026 to state nonmember banks.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation issued on Oct. 5 its list of state nonmember banks recently evaluated for compliance with the Community Reinvestment Act. The list covers evaluation ratings the FDIC assigned in July 2026.

The Community Reinvestment Act is a 1977 law that requires the FDIC to assess how well a bank meets the credit needs of its whole community, including low- and moderate-income neighborhoods, consistent with safe and sound operations. Congress required public disclosure of each evaluation and rating under the 1989 FIRREA law.

The FDIC says anyone can get a consolidated list of all state nonmember banks whose evaluations have been made public since July 1, 1990, with their ratings, from its Public Information Center at 877-275-3342 or 703-562-2200. An individual bank's evaluation is available from the bank on request, which the bank is required by law to provide, or from the same FDIC office.

For a customer, the rating is one data point about a bank's local lending record, such as mortgages and small-business loans in your area. It does not measure a bank's safety, and it is separate from FDIC deposit insurance. The FDIC release itself contains the list as an attachment, and it does not summarize the results.

title: Fed Minutes: September Rate Increase Was Unanimous, Core Inflation Was 3.4%
description: Minutes released Oct. 7 show the Fed raised its target range to 3.75% to 4% and moved the primary credit rate to 4%.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Reserve released the minutes of its Sept. 15-16 policy meeting on Oct. 7. They show the Federal Open Market Committee raised the target range for the federal funds rate to 3-3/4 to 4 percent. The record lists no votes against the action, with twelve members voting for it and none against.

Alongside the decision, the Board of Governors voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 3.90 percent and the primary credit rate to 4.0 percent, both effective Sept. 17. The minutes say markets had priced in high odds of a 25 basis point increase and that investors placed considerable probability on at least that much tightening by year-end.

On the economy, the staff estimated core PCE inflation, which leaves out energy and many food prices, stayed at 3.4 percent in August, higher than a year earlier. The unemployment rate moved down to 4.1 percent in July and August. Participants described growth as solid in the first half of the year, and the minutes call risks to the employment and growth forecasts roughly balanced.

For households, a higher federal funds target generally pushes up the rates on credit cards, home equity lines and other variable-rate debt. The minutes do not forecast any particular loan rate, and they describe committee discussion, not a promise of future increases. People carrying variable-rate balances may want to check their current rate and any scheduled adjustments.

title: FTC Explains What Parents Can Do When an Explicit Image of Their Child Is Shared Online
description: The consumer alert covers reporting to police and NCMEC, platform takedown requests under the Take It Down Act, and the 48-hour window.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The FTC published a consumer alert on Oct. 7 for parents whose child's explicit image has been shared online. It says possessing or sharing explicit images of children can be a serious crime, including AI-generated deepfakes, and that parents should report the person responsible and get platforms to remove the images quickly.

To report the person, the FTC lists three routes: the local police department, the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children's CyberTipline or 1-800-843-5678, and the FBI at 1-800-CALL-FBI or a local field office. NCMEC analysts make a report available to the appropriate law enforcement agency.

To get the image taken down, the FTC says the Take It Down Act requires covered platforms to give parents an easy way to request removal of explicit images of a child. With an account, use the report option on or near the image, often in the three-dot menu. Without one, check the platform's help center. If a covered platform does not remove the image within 48 hours, report it to the FTC at TakeItDown.ftc.gov.

The alert also points to NCMEC's Take It Down service, which creates a hash, a digital fingerprint of the image, to help stop it from appearing on other sites. The FTC says acting quickly can make a meaningful difference, and its TakeItDown.ftc.gov page links to support and guidance.

title: FTC Closes T-Shirt Pricing Probe After Gildan and S&S Change Contract
description: The agency says the amended agreement no longer limits Gildan's pricing to other wholesale distributors.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Trade Commission said Oct. 8 it has closed an investigation into T-shirt maker Gildan Activewear and wholesale distributor S&S Holdings after the two companies changed their partnership agreement. The FTC had examined whether the old contract barred Gildan from giving S&S's competitors certain prices and discounts.

The agency looked at Gildan under Section 2(a) of the Robinson-Patman Act, which bars certain price discrimination, and at S&S under Section 2(f), which covers knowingly inducing or receiving prohibited discrimination. Following the inquiry, the contract now says nothing in it restricts Gildan's discretion to set prices or offer partnership support to any other North American wholesale distributor.

The FTC posted a public letter from Gildan confirming the amendment. It called the matter a follow-up to last week's settlement with Southern Glazer's Wine and Spirits, which it described as the first Robinson-Patman case resolved by a federal enforcement agency in more than 20 years.

For shoppers the effect is indirect. The FTC's reasoning is that when small distributors and retailers can get equivalent discounts, they compete better, and that can mean more choice and lower prices. The release does not promise any price cut, and the agency did not announce a fine or refund in this case.

title: FTC Warns 24 Healthcare Companies: Meeting CMS Price Rules Is Not Enough
description: Letters say incomplete or inaccurate prices can be deceptive, including when physician or facility fees are left out.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson sent letters on Oct. 5 to 24 of the largest healthcare services companies, reminding them they must give patients timely, accurate and complete price information. The FTC says failing to do so can be an unfair or deceptive practice under Section 5 of the FTC Act.

The letters focus on routine, non-emergency care scheduled in advance. They say compliance with the price transparency rules from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services is a baseline, not a safe harbor from FTC Act liability. A price disclosure can still be deceptive if it is incomplete, such as when it leaves out physician or facility fees or covers only part of the expected course of care, because patients may reasonably believe they were told the total cost.

The FTC also says leaving out a price can mislead, and that inaccurate figures are misleading too. It adds that failing to give price information far enough ahead of a scheduled service can be unfair if consumers cannot compare providers and cannot reasonably avoid the harm.

The letters are warnings, not enforcement actions or findings against any company, and the release does not name the 24 recipients. Chairman Ferguson urged them to review their price disclosures and fix problems quickly. For patients, the practical point is to ask for the full expected cost, including professional fees, before scheduled care, and to get the answer in writing.

title: FTC and Two States Sue Lens.com Over a "Taxes & Fees" Charge at Checkout
description: The complaint says the charge often doubles the advertised price of contact lenses. The case will be decided by a court.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Trade Commission, with the Utah and Nevada attorneys general, sued contact lens seller Lens.com on Oct. 2. The joint complaint, filed in federal court in Nevada, also names owner Cary Samourkachian and an affiliated company, Speed Commerce. The agencies allege the company advertised low prices and then added a mandatory "Taxes & fees" charge at checkout.

The complaint says the charge routinely doubles the advertised price and has cost consumers hundreds of millions of dollars. It also alleges that the line item sits below the visible part of the checkout screen, so shoppers who click the prominent Continue button never see it. And it says the label suggests state sales tax, though many states exempt contact lenses from sales tax or have none.

The agencies also allege the same pricing was used to enroll people in AutoRefill, a recurring-shipment plan, without clearly disclosing the charge before collecting billing details. They say the company did not clearly disclose how to cancel or the deadline to cancel before a future shipment.

The FTC, Utah and Nevada allege violations of the FTC Act, the Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act, the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act and state consumer laws. The FTC notes that it files a complaint when it has reason to believe the law is being broken, and a court decides the case. No refund program has been announced. If you buy lenses online, compare the final total at checkout, not the advertised price, and check the cancellation terms before joining any auto-refill plan.

title: GOAT Customers: FTC Is Mailing Refund Checks to 6,205 Buyers
description: The FTC says it is sending more than $100,000 to shoppers who were denied promised refunds. Checks must be cashed within 90 days.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Trade Commission said Tuesday it is sending more than $100,000 to people who bought from GOAT, an online marketplace for sneakers, apparel and accessories. The money goes to 6,205 customers who have not yet been paid in a settlement over refund and shipping practices.

The FTC's 2024 complaint said GOAT did not ship some priority-processing orders as fast as it promised. It also said buyers were not offered the choice to accept a delay or cancel for a prompt refund, as the agency's Mail, Internet or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule requires. A second claim covered GOAT's Buyer Protection promise: the FTC said the company often denied refunds for items that were fake, wrong or not as described, or gave only a partial refund or store credit.

In 2025, GOAT refunded more than $736,000 directly to affected customers. This latest round covers people who were left out of that earlier payout. Most will get a check in the mail, and the rest will get a PayPal payment. The FTC says check recipients have 90 days to cash the check, and PayPal recipients have 30 days to redeem the payment.

Questions go to the refund administrator, JND Legal Administration, at 1-888-970-2410, or to the FTC's refund page. The agency says it never requires anyone to pay money or give account information to receive a payment. If a message about a refund asks for either, treat it as a scam and contact the administrator through the number the FTC lists.

title: HUD Opens Fair Housing Investigation Into Wells Fargo Homeownership Programs
description: HUD says it sent the bank's CEO a letter examining its efforts to increase Black homeownership.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development said Oct. 7 that Secretary Scott Turner launched an investigation into Wells Fargo's initiatives to increase homeownership for Black Americans. HUD says the programs may violate the Fair Housing Act.

According to a Wall Street Journal report that HUD reposted, HUD sent Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf a letter saying it would examine whether the bank violated fair-lending laws by favoring Black or other minority homeowners. The programs and commitments in question stretch over nearly a decade. The Journal reported that Wells Fargo had no immediate comment.

HUD Assistant Secretary Craig Trainor said the Fair Housing Act forbids racial discrimination in housing and that labeling a practice a special purpose credit program does not exempt it. Secretary Turner said that even if the bank did not break the law, the practice was wrong. Those are HUD's statements, and HUD has not announced any finding.

An investigation is not a finding of a violation. HUD's page does not name any penalty, and it does not say how long the review will take. Borrowers with Wells Fargo mortgages are not told to do anything under the announcement.

title: Idaho Attorney General Lists 51 Products Recalled by CPSC in September
description: The list includes mattresses that fail flammability rules and 17 items for infants and children.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Idaho Attorney General Raul Labrador released on Oct. 7 a list of 51 hazardous products recalled by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission in September. His office says the list includes mattresses, household appliances and furniture, and seventeen items specifically designed for infants and children.

The release highlights a fire extinguisher made in China that was recalled for creating an explosion hazard and a risk of death or injury from burns. Several recalled mattresses, including Kesyup, Emerspring and WinxMatrs brands, were recalled for violating the mandatory mattress flammability standard. A children's bicycle helmet and pads set from 5Color was recalled for violating the mandatory bicycle helmet standard.

Labrador said foreign products are not always made to U.S. safety standards and urged consumers, especially those buying for children, to stay alert to recalls. His office publishes the list so families can check what they own against federal notices.

The practical step is to compare products you own with the CPSC recall listings, then follow each notice's remedy. Many recalls offer a refund, repair or replacement, and the notice names the company contact and any proof the company requires. The Idaho release is a roundup, so details such as units and remedies are in each individual CPSC notice.

title: IRS Highlights Partnership With UK Tax Authority's Whistleblower Program
description: The IRS says its whistleblower office helped HMRC set up a rewards scheme aimed at serious tax evasion by the wealthiest.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The IRS said on Oct. 7 that it is highlighting its partnership with the United Kingdom's tax whistleblower program. The IRS says its Whistleblower Office shared expertise that helped the UK program get established quickly.

The UK program, run by His Majesty's Revenue and Customs and called the Strengthened Reward Scheme, launched in November 2025. It is meant to encourage reports of serious tax avoidance and evasion involving the wealthiest individuals and largest businesses. IRS Chief Executive Frank Bisignano said the collaboration will help deter large-scale, cross-border tax evasion.

The IRS says modern evasion often relies on offshore accounts, shell companies and transfers split across countries, which are hard for investigators to trace. It says insiders such as accountants, bankers and executives can supply specific, credible information that helps tax authorities see through those structures.

The release is about cooperation between agencies. It does not announce a new reward level or filing rule for U.S. taxpayers, and it does not describe any case. People who believe they have information about large-scale tax evasion can find the IRS Whistleblower Office's process on irs.gov.

title: IRS Tip: Payment Plans, Offers in Compromise and Wage Levy Limits Under Taxpayer Rights
description: An Oct. 7 IRS tax tip lists what the right to a fair and just tax system means for people who owe.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The IRS published Tax Tip 2026-73 on Oct. 7, part of a series on the Taxpayer Bill of Rights. This one covers the right to a fair and just tax system, which includes expecting the IRS to consider facts that affect what you owe, your ability to pay and your ability to provide information on time.

The IRS lists several ways the right shows up. Taxpayers who face financial difficulty, or whose tax issue was not resolved properly through normal channels, can get help from the Taxpayer Advocate Service. Low Income Taxpayer Clinics are another source of help. Eligible taxpayers who cannot pay in full may be able to arrange a payment plan, generally paid monthly.

A taxpayer can also submit an offer in compromise, asking the IRS to settle for less than the full amount, if they believe they do not owe all or part of the debt, cannot pay it within the time allowed for collection, or would face hardship or injustice by paying in full. In reviewing an offer, the IRS uses national and local cost-of-living guidelines, but it says it will use actual expenses if the guidelines would leave a person unable to cover basic living costs.

The tip also says the IRS cannot levy or seize all of a person's wages for unpaid tax. A portion is exempt so the taxpayer can pay basic living expenses. The tip is general information, and each option has its own eligibility rules.

title: Michigan Customers: Coinbase Will Stop Sports Event Contracts and Close Positions by Oct. 10
description: The state gaming board says the deal follows similar agreements with Robinhood and Kalshi. Coinbase's appeal continues.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Michigan Gaming Control Board announced Oct. 7 that Coinbase Financial Markets has agreed to stop offering new sports-related event contracts to Michigan customers by 12 a.m. Eastern on Oct. 10, 2026. Coinbase also agreed to close any remaining open customer positions by that deadline.

The board describes the contracts as sports wagering products presented as federally regulated prediction markets. It says the agreement follows a nearly identical one with Robinhood and that Michigan has now secured agreements or court orders halting such contracts from Kalshi, Robinhood and Coinbase. The covered contracts include those traded on KalshiEX and other designated contract markets.

In return, the state agreed not to take enforcement action against Coinbase as long as it complies and while related appeals go on in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit. The board says the court denied Coinbase's request for a preliminary injunction in August 2026, and that Coinbase's appeal of that ruling is pending. The agreement does not settle the underlying legal question.

Michigan residents with open sports contract positions on Coinbase should check how and when their positions will be closed before the Oct. 10 deadline, and review their account statements afterward. The board's release does not describe how positions will be settled. It also notes gambling help is available at 1-800-GAMBLER.

title: Nebraska Sues TP-Link Over Router Security and China Ties Claims
description: The attorney general alleges deceptive marketing under state consumer law and seeks civil penalties. The company's response was not in the release.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Nebraska Attorney General Mike Hilgers filed a lawsuit Oct. 6 against TP-Link Systems Inc. under the state's Consumer Act and Uniform Deceptive Trade Practices Act. His office says TP-Link controls at least 60 percent of the U.S. retail market for Wi-Fi systems and small-office and home-office routers and sells through major retailers in Nebraska.

The complaint alleges TP-Link misled consumers by saying its routers are safe and secure and that it has severed ties to China. The attorney general says the company still depends on research, development and manufacturing in China, imports most components for its Vietnam plant from or through China, and hired a contractor with ties to the Chinese military to build that plant. He also says the products are vulnerable to exploitation by Russian intelligence.

The state seeks to stop TP-Link from making what it calls misleading claims and to inform consumers of the alleged risks. It also seeks civil penalties and fees. These are allegations in a lawsuit, and the release does not include a response from TP-Link or any court ruling.

The Nebraska release says the suit follows similar actions against makers and sellers of surveillance equipment. Consumers who own a router should keep its firmware updated and change default passwords; those steps are general advice, not part of the Nebraska filing.

title: About 110,550 PACEARTH Swing Seats Recalled After Falls and Injuries
description: Buyers on Amazon since 2017 can get a full refund after photographing the marked seat.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced on Oct. 8 a recall of about 110,550 PACEARTH swing seats sold by Pacearth Direct. The agency says the seats, metal carabiners or quick links, or webbing straps can break during use, creating a fall hazard.

Pacearth Direct has received at least 30 reports of falls, including at least nine injuries such as fractures, head injuries and bruising. The recalled product is a U-type swing seat sold in green, blue, pink, red and turquoise, with a chain coated in yellow plastic and yellow webbing straps. It was sold singly or in a pack of two.

The seats were sold on Amazon.com from May 2017 through June 2026 for between $27 and $57. The company is based in City of Industry, California, and the seats were made in China. The recall number is 27-019.

The remedy is a full refund. Buyers should stop using the swing right away. To get the refund they must write "RECALLED" on the seat with a permanent marker, take a photo that shows the PACEARTH logo, and email it to recall@pacearth.com. The CPSC consumer hotline is 800-638-2772.

title: Premier Martial Arts Franchisees May Get a Penalty-Free Exit Under FTC Settlement
description: Proposed orders require $1.85 million in payments and let certain franchisees cancel without penalty.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Trade Commission announced Oct. 5 that Premier Franchising Group, the franchisor behind Premier Martial Arts, and its former franchise sales organization, Franchise Fastlane, agreed to proposed settlements totaling $1.85 million. The FTC says the companies misled buyers about what the franchise could earn and broke the agency's Franchise Rule.

According to the complaint, the companies claimed that people with no martial arts background could profitably run one or more studios on a semi-absentee basis, working under 15 hours a week. The FTC says more than 200 consumers, including veterans, paid an initial franchise fee of $49,500 or more. They then spent hundreds of thousands of dollars building and running studios, and many took on significant debt.

The complaint also says Premier's 2020 to 2022 franchise disclosure documents reported strong studio earnings without a reasonable basis to say new franchisees could match them, because existing studios were often larger than the ones new owners were advised to open. It adds that sales staff made income claims that were not in the disclosure documents.

Under the proposed orders, Premier Franchising Group faces a $3,875,424 judgment that is partly suspended once it pays $650,000, and Franchise Fastlane will pay $1.2 million. The money is meant to compensate franchisees. Premier must also send certain franchisees a notice offering the right to cancel their agreements with no penalty. The orders carry the force of law only once the federal court in the Eastern District of Tennessee approves them.

title: 43 States Seek Approval of $400 Million Sandoz Generic Drug Settlement
description: Buyers of generic prescriptions between May 2009 and December 2019 may be eligible for compensation.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Washington Attorney General Nick Brown announced Oct. 6 that he joined a coalition of 43 states and territories asking a federal court to approve a $400 million settlement with Sandoz Inc. and Fougera Pharmaceuticals over alleged generic drug price-fixing. The motion for preliminary approval was filed Oct. 1 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Connecticut.

The states allege the two manufacturers took part in long-running conspiracies to inflate prices and reduce competition. The settlement also resolves allegations that Sandoz's international affiliates, Novartis AG, Sandoz AG and Sandoz Group AG, took part and moved assets to avoid liability. Sandoz agreed to injunctive terms that include internal reforms to support fair competition. Washington's share is more than $12 million.

Consumers who bought a generic prescription drug between May 2009 and December 2019 may be eligible for compensation. Washington says people can check eligibility at www.AGGenericDrugs.com, by calling 1-866-290-0182, or by emailing info@AGGenericDrugs.com. Businesses in Washington and Idaho that indirectly bought or reimbursed the drugs at issue may also qualify, through the site's corporate entities page.

The court has not yet approved the deal, so no payments are scheduled. This settlement follows earlier ones with Glenmark, Lannett, Bausch, Apotex and Heritage, which are part of a series of generic drug antitrust cases the states began in 2016.

title: SEC and Regulators Warn Investors About Relationship and Impersonation Scams
description: A joint bulletin for World Investor Week urges caution about rising investment fraud.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced Oct. 5 that it issued a joint investor bulletin with other U.S. financial regulators as part of World Investor Week. The bulletin urges investors to be resilient as economic conditions change and to watch for rising relationship investment scams and impersonation scams.

The SEC coordinated the U.S. effort with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, the Securities Investor Protection Corporation, the National Futures Association and the North American Securities Administrators Association. World Investor Week is an effort led by the International Organization of Securities Commissions, and this year is its tenth anniversary.

SEC Chairman Paul Atkins urged investors to use the agency's Investor.gov site, which offers free investor education and planning tools, and to stay alert for scams. The release does not describe individual scam cases or give loss figures.

The practical step in the announcement is to check resources before sending money to someone you met online or to someone claiming to represent a firm. Investor.gov is the site the SEC points people to for that kind of verification.

title: Southern Glazer's Settles FTC Price Discrimination Case Over Wine and Spirits
description: The order covers sales to five large chains in 26 states and lasts six years under an independent monitor.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Trade Commission announced Oct. 2 a settlement with Southern Glazer's Wine and Spirits, the largest U.S. wine and spirits distributor. It resolves a 2024 FTC lawsuit alleging Southern charged independent retailers more than competing large chains for identical bottles, even when stores were a few blocks apart.

The proposed stipulated order covers nearly all of Southern's wine and spirits sales to the five largest chain retailers in 26 states. It targets paired transactions, where Southern sells a product to a chain and, at about the same time, to a nearby independent retailer at a much higher price. A violation requires significant price discrimination above a threshold based on state operating costs, and recurring discrimination of more than $5,000 in total over 12 months.

If those conditions are met, Southern can fix the problem by paying the independent retailer 1.5 times the total price difference. If it does not, the FTC can sue, and a win would require Southern to pay double the price differences. The order lasts six years and is overseen by an independent monitor.

The FTC called it the first Robinson-Patman Act case resolved by a federal enforcement agency in more than 20 years, and says the aim is to help small businesses compete and give shoppers access to lower-priced wine and spirits at local retailers. The release does not say shelf prices will fall or by how much. The order has the force of law only after the court in the Central District of California approves it.

title: SSA Audit: Thousands of Disabled Beneficiaries Weren't Told They Could Get Higher Retirement Pay
description: The inspector general estimates about $84 million in benefits was at stake for people whose disability pay is reduced by other benefits.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Social Security Administration's Office of the Inspector General released an audit on Oct. 6 about disabled beneficiaries who may qualify for higher retirement benefits. It looked at people whose disability payments the Social Security Act requires SSA to reduce because they also receive workers' compensation or public disability benefits.

Auditors estimated SSA did not notify 8,726 of these beneficiaries that they could file for higher retirement benefits. It notified another 3,659 but did not properly record their decisions not to file or their reasons. The inspector general estimated these groups could have been entitled to about $84 million in additional benefits.

The report adds that statutory limits prevent SSA employees from issuing those payments, so the amount is an estimate of what was at stake, not money on its way to anyone. Auditors also found SSA may be able to pay an estimated $41 million to 4,785 other beneficiaries who already filed for retirement benefits but did not get the correct, higher amount.

The problem is not new. A 2015 audit flagged the same gap, and SSA agreed to fix it and automated part of its notice process. The new follow-up found that notification and documentation problems persisted. If you receive disability benefits that are reduced because of workers' compensation or a public disability payment, ask SSA directly whether a retirement benefit would pay more, and keep a record of the answer.

title: SSI Recipients: Report Changes by the 10th of the Month to Avoid Overpayments
description: Social Security's Oct. 7 notice lists what must be reported and the five ways to report wages.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Social Security Administration sent a note to advocates on Oct. 7 asking them to remind clients on Supplemental Security Income to report changes quickly, in order to reduce improper payments. SSI is a needs-based program, so changes in income, resources or living arrangements can change a payment or eligibility.

SSA says changes must be reported no later than the 10th day of the month after they happen. Reportable changes include income from wages, self-employment, benefits, pensions or cash from friends or relatives; moves and changes in household members, rent or utility costs; bank accounts, cash, property and other assets; marital status; citizenship or immigration status; absences from the U.S. of 30 consecutive days or more; and eligibility for other benefits. The resource limits SSA lists are $2,000 for an individual and $3,000 for a couple.

Married recipients who live with a spouse must report changes that affect the spouse. For a child on SSI, changes involving the child's parents must be reported. Workers must report wages by the 10th of each month, though SSA encourages reporting by the 6th of the month after payday to lower the risk of an overpayment.

Wages can be reported through an employer using the Payroll Information Exchange, a personal my Social Security account, the SSA Mobile Wage Reporting app, the automated telephone wage reporting system, or a local office. Before using an automated option for the first time, or after changing employers, call SSA at 1-800-772-1213 (TTY 1-800-325-0778), Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 7 p.m., to give employer information. Keep a record of each report you make.

title: Texas Attorney General Opens Investigation Into Kids' Underwear Makers Over Chemicals
description: Civil investigative demands went to Hanes and Fruit of the Loom. The release does not report any finding of harm.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton announced on Oct. 6 an investigation into major children's clothing brands over the possible presence of toxic chemicals in materials used in children's undergarments. His office issued Civil Investigative Demands to Hanes and Fruit of the Loom.

The release says cheaper synthetic fabrics such as polyester, rayon and spandex can involve plastic-derived materials or chemical-heavy manufacturing. It says synthetic fabrics can shed microplastics, and that chemicals such as bisphenols, phthalates, PFAS and parabens used in textile manufacturing have been associated with endocrine disruption, infertility, cancer and other health concerns.

Those statements describe research and concerns cited by the attorney general's office. The release does not say any product tested positive, does not allege that either company broke the law, and does not include a response from Hanes or Fruit of the Loom. A civil investigative demand is a request for documents and information, not a finding or a lawsuit.

Paxton said he wants to make sure children's necessities do not contain harmful materials. Parents who want to reduce exposure can check care labels and brand statements about testing, but nothing in the announcement tells shoppers to stop buying a product or to seek a refund.

title: Treasury Says Payment Checks Returned $175 Million Before It Reached Recipients
description: Treasury reports it screened 1.1 billion federal payments worth about $3.7 trillion in fiscal 2026.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Treasury Department and the Bureau of the Fiscal Service reported Oct. 6 on fiscal year 2026 results from their fraud and improper payment prevention work. Treasury says its Do Not Pay service now reaches about 99 percent of federal programs, up from about 4 percent at the end of fiscal 2025.

Treasury says it screened more than 2.3 billion records against Do Not Pay data sources, up from 641 million the year before, and added nine datasets, including company registration data and select verification against Social Security's Numident file. It also set up a new payment verification process.

Under that process, Treasury says it screened more than 1.1 billion federal payments totaling about $3.7 trillion. It identified and returned about 13,500 payments worth $175 million. Treasury piloted checks of bank account ownership and of whether Taxpayer Identification Numbers are present and correctly formatted, and says those checks became fully operational on Sept. 30, 2026.

These are Treasury's own figures, and the release does not say how many returned payments were later found to be legitimate or corrected. For people who receive federal payments, the practical point is that a mismatched bank account or tax ID can now cause a payment to be stopped. Keep your bank details and taxpayer ID current with the agency that pays you.

title: Trump Accounts: What the White House Says About 70 Million Children's Accounts
description: The administration says parents must claim an account to manage it and receive the $1,000 seed deposit for eligible children.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The White House said on Oct. 7 that nearly 70 million Trump Accounts have been created, including more than 60 million through automatic enrollment. It says every child under 18 with a Social Security number now has an account in their name. These are the administration's figures, taken from its own release.

According to the White House, a parent or guardian has to claim the account through the Trump Accounts App. Claiming lets them manage the account, unlock contributions from family and friends, and receive the one-time $1,000 seed contribution for eligible children. The release says more than $4.5 billion has been deposited since the July 4 launch, including $1.3 billion in seed contributions, over $600 million from family and friends and $2.6 billion in philanthropic gifts.

On contributions, the White House says family and friends can add up to $5,000 a year. Employers can contribute up to $2,500 a year, within the overall $5,000 annual limit. It says more than 70 companies have committed to contributions for employees and that an estimated 80 percent of accounts are linked to families earning less than $200,000 a year.

The page also projects balances growing to an estimated half a million dollars by retirement, which is a projection, not a guaranteed outcome. It does not detail the withdrawal rules, fees or investment options. Families should read the program terms on the official site before moving money, and should be wary of any message that asks for a Social Security number or payment to claim an account.

title: Sentencing Shows How a Thief Tried to Take a Deceased Seattle Resident's Home and Accounts
description: A forged power of attorney, bank logins and brokerage takeovers were stopped by a niece and fraud restrictions.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: A federal court in Seattle sentenced a 36-year-old Carnation, Washington, man to three years in prison on Oct. 5 for wire fraud, access device fraud and aggravated identity theft, according to the Labor Department's Office of Inspector General. Tyler Lee Berens pleaded guilty in July. The case combined pandemic benefit fraud with an attempt to take over a dead man's estate.

Prosecutors say that from 2020 Berens filed false pandemic unemployment claims in 19 states and collected $148,206 from six of them, and also got a $17,500 Paycheck Protection Program loan. Starting about two years later, they say he posed as the authorized agent of a deceased elderly Seattle resident and tried to take over the home, bank accounts and a stock portfolio, in total more than half a million dollars.

The release says he sent a real estate agent a forged power of attorney and accepted an offer on the house, until the victim's niece was alerted and reported it. He then accessed the victim's bank accounts and got a debit card. After fraud restrictions were added, he emailed while impersonating the dead victim to try to lift them. He also tried to move money from the victim's brokerage accounts and to liquidate over $235,000 of stock.

For families settling an estate, the case shows why to notify banks, brokerages and credit bureaus of a death promptly and to be careful with who holds paperwork such as a power of attorney, which ends at death. The release does not offer a checklist, so check with a probate attorney or the institutions involved about their own procedures.

title: West Virginia: FEMA Individual Assistance Approved for Fayette, Harrison and Kanawha Counties
description: Residents hit by the Aug. 14-18 storms can apply online or by phone. FEMA kept its denial for Boone and Logan counties.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: West Virginia Gov. Patrick Morrisey announced Oct. 7 that additional federal disaster assistance has been approved for the state. The approvals cover storms and flooding this summer.

Individual Assistance was approved for Fayette, Harrison and Kanawha counties after the severe storms and flooding from Aug. 14 through 18. The governor's office says that assistance can help eligible residents with temporary housing, home repairs and other uninsured or underinsured disaster-related losses. Residents of those counties can apply at DisasterAssistance.gov, through the FEMA mobile app, or by calling the FEMA Helpline at 800-621-3362.

Public Assistance was approved for Barbour, Doddridge, Lewis, Pendleton, Pleasants, Randolph, Ritchie, Tucker, Tyler, Upshur and Wetzel counties after storms, flooding and landslides that began July 21. That program pays, on a cost-share basis, for emergency work, debris removal and repair of public infrastructure such as roads and utilities, not for private homes. Individual Assistance had already been approved for Lewis, Pleasants, Ritchie and Upshur counties for the July storms.

FEMA also reaffirmed its denial of Individual Assistance for Boone and Logan counties after the June flooding, rejecting the state's appeal. The governor said he is disappointed and the state will keep looking for other resources for those communities. The release does not give payment amounts or an application deadline, so check DisasterAssistance.gov for current terms.

title: Cleo AI Customers: FTC Will Pay 2.1 Million People Through PayPal Starting Oct. 27
description: The FTC says $15.8 million goes to customers who paid for instant cash advances. Eligibility emails go out by Oct. 26.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Trade Commission said Thursday it is sending more than $15.8 million to customers of Cleo AI, a cash advance app. The agency plans to pay 2,124,796 people who paid for eligible instant cash advances.

The FTC’s March 2025 complaint alleged that Cleo advertised access to "hundreds of dollars" in cash advances when almost no one received amounts close to that. It also alleged hidden fees for same-day or instant advances that often arrived the next day, and subscriptions that were hard to cancel.

Eligible customers will get an email between now and October 26, 2026. The FTC will begin sending PayPal payments on October 27, and recipients should redeem them within 30 days. The refund administrator is Rust Consulting at 877-788-4958.
The FTC says it never requires anyone to pay money or give account information to receive a payment. A message that asks for either is not from the refund program.

sources.label: FTC: FTC Returns More than $15.8 Million to Consumers Misled by Cash Advance App Company Cleo AI (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Greenway Auto Group Must Advertise the Real Price Under FTC Settlement
description: The FTC says Greenway charged an average of more than $3,350 over the advertised price in over 92% of sales.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The FTC announced Thursday that Greenway Auto Group agreed to a proposed order requiring its price ads to prominently show the actual price a buyer must pay, excluding only charges the government requires. The agency had sued, alleging the dealer group advertised prices thousands of dollars below what it charged.

According to the complaint, Greenway charged more than $3,350 over the advertised price, on average, in over 92% of transactions. The added items included administrative, dealer, delivery and processing fees, plus packages and penalties. Some advertised prices also reflected rebates and discounts that only a subset of buyers could get.

The FTC also alleges Greenway sent mailers saying recipients had won thousands of dollars in cash prizes redeemable at a dealership, and that the prizes were not real. The proposed order bans deceptive prize mailers and misrepresenting whether fees, taxes, products or services are optional or required.

The complaint says the FTC warned Greenway in a March 2026 letter, and the company then added assurances of price transparency to its websites while continuing the same pricing. The stipulated order was filed in federal court in Orlando and has the force of law once the judge approves and signs it. For car shoppers, the practical point is to ask for an out-the-door price in writing before visiting.

sources.label: FTC: FTC Secures Settlement with Auto Dealership Group in Price Transparency Win for Consumers (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Generic Drug Price-Fixing: New Yorkers Have Until March 8, 2027 to Claim
description: Ascend and Mayne will pay $400,000 and $650,000. Buyers of listed generics from May 2009 to December 2019 may qualify.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: New York Attorney General Letitia James announced Thursday that Ascend Laboratories and Mayne Pharma are paying a combined $1 million to settle state claims over a generic drug price-fixing scheme. Mayne will pay $650,000 and Ascend $400,000. A coalition of 47 other attorneys general joined the settlements.

New Yorkers who bought a generic prescription drug listed on the settlement website between May 2009 and December 2019 may be eligible for compensation. The claim deadline is March 8, 2027. Claims can be filed at AGGenericDrugs.com, by email at info@aggenericdrugs.com, or by phone at 1-866-290-0182.

A third company, Citron Pharma, settled on non-monetary terms because it has stopped doing business. The announcement says the funds will go to affected consumers across the coalition states, and each settling company agreed to antitrust compliance reforms including annual training.
The settlements are part of three multistate lawsuits against generic drug makers. The announcement lists earlier settlements, including $400 million from Sandoz earlier this month.

sources.label: New York Attorney General: AG James Secures Over $1 Million from Ascend Laboratories and Mayne Pharma (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Texas Roofing Company Ordered to Pay $1.5 Million; Victims Can Get Restitution
description: The judgment finds 27 deceptive-practice violations and sets aside at least $500,000 for victims.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton announced Thursday a judgment against Rubinsky Roofing LLC, a North Texas company, and its owner Gilad Rubinsky. The state sued in May. The judgment holds the company liable for 27 violations of the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act. Five involved people 65 or older.

The attorney general’s office says the violations include taking insurance money or personal funds for unnecessary or sham repairs. In some cases customers paid for roofing work that was never started or finished.
The company will pay more than $1.5 million in civil penalties, and at least another $500,000 will go to victims. The judgment permanently bars the company and its owner from the practices at issue.

Affected customers do not need to do anything yet. The company must hand over names and contact information, and the Consumer Protection Division says it will contact victims within 15 days of receiving it with instructions for claiming restitution.

sources.label: Texas Attorney General: Attorney General Ken Paxton Secures Repayment for Texans Who Were Scammed by Rubinsky Roofing Company (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: ONTHEWEI Baby Bath Seats Recalled: Stop Using Them and Ask for a Refund
description: CPSC says the seats can tip over and violate the federal bath seat standard. About 2,140 were sold on Amazon.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced a recall Thursday of about 2,140 ONTHEWEI baby bath seats. CPSC says they violate the mandatory standard for infant bath seats because they are unstable and can tip over in use, which poses a risk of serious injury or death from drowning. No incidents were reported.

The seats come in gray, pink, blue and mist green, with detachable restraint arms and suction cups underneath. A label on the back reads "Model No: MY002" and "Date of manufacturer: 2026/1/10". They sold on Amazon.com in April 2026 for $40 to $50.

Owners should stop using the seat now and email ONTHEWEI at onthewei@outlook.com for a full refund. To qualify, they must write "RECALLED" on the front, remove the back rest and arm restraints, cut the three suction cups, and send a photo of the marked seat. Then dispose of it.
A bath seat is not a safety device, and a child should never be left alone in the tub. This is recall 27-018.

sources.label: CPSC: ONTHEWEI Recalls Baby Bath Seats Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death to Children from Drowning (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Romorgniz Six-Drawer Dressers Recalled: 12,078 Sold on Amazon, Refund Available
description: CPSC says unanchored dressers can tip over and violate the STURDY Act standard. No injuries were reported.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced a recall Thursday of about 12,078 Romorgniz six-drawer dressers. CPSC says they are unstable if not anchored to the wall, creating tip-over and entrapment hazards for children, and that they violate the safety standard required by the STURDY Act. No injuries were reported.

The wooden dressers came in white and black, about 27.6 inches wide, 15.6 inches long and 43.2 inches tall, and weigh 73.3 pounds. They sold on Amazon.com from May 2025 through August 2026 for $100 to $170.

Owners should stop using the dresser if it is not anchored, keep it where children cannot get to it, and contact Romorgniz for a full refund at Romorgnizrecall@outlook.com or through the recall page on romorgniz.store. The firm asks for photos showing "RECALLED" written on the top, front and sides and the drawers removed. Then dispose of it. This is recall 27-020.

sources.label: CPSC: Romorgniz Recalls Six-Drawer Dressers Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Tip-Over and Entrapment Hazards (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Snow Peak Recalls Takibi Propane Inserts: Lava Rocks Can Explode When Heated
description: About 100 units sold for about $350. Owners can get a refund, or keep the insert and get replacement rocks.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced Thursday that Snow Peak USA is recalling about 100 Takibi propane inserts with lava rocks, model ST-332-US. CPSC says the rocks can ignite and explode when heated in the insert, which poses a risk of serious injury or death from burns and fire. The firm has one report of exploding lava rocks, with minor property damage and no injuries.

The insert lets the Pack & Carry Fireplace L (ST-032) and XL (ST-034) run on propane. The fireplaces themselves are not recalled. The model number is on the packaging and in the manual. The product sold on snowpeak.com in July 2026 for about $350.

Owners should stop using the insert and rocks now. Snow Peak will provide a prepaid label for a full refund. Anyone who wants to keep the insert can instead get replacement lava rocks, and should not use the insert until they arrive. Contact Snow Peak USA at 888-424-4916 or info@snowpeak.com. This is recall 27-021.

sources.label: CPSC: Snow Peak Recalls Propane Fireplace Inserts and Lava Rocks Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Burn and Fire Hazards (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: DR Power Recalls 42,860 Trimmer Mowers After 19 Fire Reports; Repair Is Free
description: CPSC says grass and debris can build up and ignite. Two minor injuries were reported.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced a recall Thursday of about 42,860 DR Power Equipment Pilot and Premier walk-behind trimmer mowers, plus about 340 sold in Canada. CPSC says grass and debris can accumulate in the machine and ignite. DR Power has received 19 reports of fires, including two reports of minor injuries such as blisters on hands and feet.

The mowers are orange and black with the DR Power logo. The recalled model numbers on the side of the frame are T4X1076DMN, T4X1076DMNR, T4X1076DMNSD, T4X1176DMN, T4X1176DMN-1, T4X1176DMNR, TR43076DMN and TR43076DMNR, all serial numbers. They sold at Ace, TSC, Bomgaars, other hardware stores and drpower.com from November 2022 through July 2026 for $380 to $550.

Owners should stop using the mower and contact DR Power for a free repair kit at 800-854-3194 or recall@drpower.com. Anyone who is not comfortable installing it can ask for free installation by an authorized dealer.

sources.label: CPSC: DR Power Equipment Recalls Pilot and Premier Trimmer Mowers Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Fire and Burn Hazards (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Van Rysel GRVL AF Bikes Recalled Because the Front Wheel Can Come Loose
description: About 1,150 gravel bikes. The free repair is done at REI Co-op stores.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced a recall Thursday of about 1,150 Van Rysel GRVL AF bicycles sold by Decathlon America. CPSC says the front lock nut can loosen during use, so the front wheel can loosen or dislodge, which is a crash hazard.

The recall covers four adult gravel bike models: 8911304 (Sword Brown), 8911305 (Apex Beige), 8911308 (Sword Pink) and 8929130 (GRX Black), in sizes x-small through x-large. The model name and Product ID are on the barcode sticker near the bottom bracket. Affected bikes have a Product ID on the label under the frame that begins with 5.

Owners should stop riding and take the bike to an REI Co-op store for a free inspection and repair of the front fork assembly. Anyone who cannot get to REI can call Decathlon America at 415-408-5494 or email support.america@decathlon.com.

sources.label: CPSC: Decathlon America Recalls Van Rysel GRVL AF Bicycles Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Crash Hazard (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Giant Recalls LED-Light Keys on SureLock Bike Locks Over Button Battery Risk
description: The keys do not meet the federal button battery standard. The refund is $5, and the lock itself stays usable.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced a recall Thursday of about 3,630 LED-light keys included with certain Giant SureLock bike lock sets, plus 1,395 in Canada. CPSC says the keys violate the mandatory standard for products with button cell batteries because children can get to the battery, and that the packaging and product lack the warnings required under Reese’s Law.

Only black-and-white LED-light keys made after March 2023 are included, and the affected serial numbers are on the underside of the lock. The lock and the non-LED keys that come in the set are not part of the recall, and owners can keep using them.

Owners should stop using the LED key. Giant will pay a $5 refund when the key is brought to an authorized Giant retailer, along with either the full lock or a photo of the lock serial number to confirm it is covered. Contact Giant at 866-458-2555 or Recall@GiantBicycle.com. Swallowed button batteries can cause serious internal chemical burns, so keep the key away from children until it is returned.

sources.label: CPSC: Giant Bicycle Recalls LED-Light Keys Included with SureLock Bike Lock Sets Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Battery Ingestion (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: The Conqueror Recalls Avengers Infinity Gauntlet Medals Over Loose Magnets
description: About 476 medals sold in March to May 2026 for about $50. Choose a refund or a replacement.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced a recall Thursday of about 476 Avengers Infinity Gauntlet medals sold by The Conqueror. CPSC says the medals violate the mandatory standard for magnets because high-powered magnets can detach and be swallowed. The firm has received three reports of magnets detaching. When more than one magnet is swallowed, they can attract each other or metal objects and cause intestinal injuries, blood poisoning and death.

The gold medal has colorful gems and comes in a black Marvel Avengers package. It was awarded for completing the Infinity Gauntlet virtual challenge on the Conqueror App, and sold through theconqueror.events and the app from March through May 2026 for about $50.

Owners should stop using the medal and contact The Conqueror at 833-799-0368 or support@theconqueror.events for a full refund or a replacement. To qualify, cut the ribbon from the medal, write "RECALLED" on the medal and ribbon, throw them away, and email a photo. This is recall 27-022.

sources.label: CPSC: The Conqueror Recalls Avengers Medals Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Magnet Ingestion (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Gardeners Basics Recalls Broccoli Sprouting Seeds Over Possible Salmonella
description: The one-pound bags sold on Amazon, Walmart, TikTok Shop, eBay and Etsy. Throw them out; no return is required.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Gardeners Basics of Spanish Fork, Utah, announced Thursday it is recalling one-pound bags of Waltham 29 Broccoli Sprouting Seeds because they may be contaminated with Salmonella. The FDA posted the company announcement and does not endorse the product or company.

The company says its supplier notified it on September 26, 2026 that bulk lot #W4105 was recalled after the FDA found Salmonella in a sample. The seeds were also used by a sprout grower whose finished product was part of an FDA investigation into a multistate foodborne illness outbreak. As of October 6, Gardeners Basics had no illness reports tied to this product.

The seeds come in a white and green resealable pouch, net weight 1 pound (454 g), UPC 848137042889, marked "Packed for 2027". They were sold online through Amazon, gardenersbasics.com, TikTok Shop, Walmart, eBay and Etsy. Sales have stopped.

Do not eat the seeds or any sprouts grown from them. Seal them and any sprouts in a bag and throw them away. No return is required, and buyers who have not already been refunded can contact the company for a refund.

sources.label: FDA: Gardeners Basics Recalls Waltham 29 Broccoli Sprouting Seeds Due to Possible Salmonella Contamination (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: SEC Says California Adviser Gave Himself the Winning Trades and Clients the Losers
description: The SEC charged Darren Caris and his firm over alleged "cherry-picking" from December 2023 to April 2024. The allegations are unproven.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission has charged Darren J. Caris and his Encinitas, California firm, Caris Investment Partners, with defrauding clients through an alleged "cherry-picking" scheme. The SEC announced the case October 8, 2026. The complaint was filed October 6 in federal court in San Diego. The charges are allegations, and the defendants have not been found liable.

According to the complaint, from December 2023 to April 2024 Caris placed trades through his firm’s block trading account, then later in the day assigned the profitable trades to his own account and the unprofitable ones to some clients. The SEC also alleges Caris and the firm made false or misleading statements to clients and prospects about how trades were allocated, how his personal trading conflicts were managed, and why they moved to a different broker-dealer custodian.

The SEC charges violations of the antifraud provisions of the Securities Act, the Exchange Act and the Investment Advisers Act. It is asking for permanent injunctions, disgorgement with prejudgment interest, and civil penalties.
For people who use an adviser, the practical step is to ask how the firm allocates block trades and whether the adviser trades for his own account.

sources.label: SEC: Darren J. Caris and Caris Investment Partners, Inc., Litigation Release No. 26669 (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Texas Ponzi Case: Two Men Agree to Final Judgments in $91 Million Scheme
description: The SEC says the "Vanguard JV Cash Program" raised at least $91 million from more than 200 investors. Conner must pay about $10.4 million and Welsh about $1.7 million.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced October 7, 2026 that a federal court in Texas has entered final consent judgments against Robert D. Welsh and Caedrynn E. Conner. The court entered them on September 28. They had been charged in April 2025 with their roles in an alleged Ponzi scheme. They consented without admitting the allegations.

According to the SEC’s complaint, between May 2021 and February 2024, Kenneth W. Alexander II and Welsh ran a scheme called the Vanguard JV Cash Program, with Conner’s alleged help. It raised at least $91 million from more than 200 investors. The complaint says it was promoted as a highly profitable international bond trading business, but investor money was used to make payments to other investors.

The judgments permanently bar both men from violating key securities antifraud laws and from taking part in offering or selling securities, except for their own personal accounts. Welsh was ordered to pay disgorgement of $1,062,069, prejudgment interest of $168,077 and a civil penalty of $450,000, which totals $1,680,146. Conner was ordered to pay disgorgement of $8,575,250, prejudgment interest of $1,357,072 and a civil penalty of $500,000, which totals $10,432,322.

The case is a reminder of the usual warning signs: steady high returns, a promoter who is vague about where the money comes from, and returns that depend on new investors. The SEC’s release lists the court case number as 4:25-cv-00446 in the Eastern District of Texas.

sources.label: SEC: Robert D. Welsh and Caedrynn E. Conner, Litigation Release No. 26668 (Oct. 7, 2026)

title: SEC Wins Final Judgments in Boiler-Room Microcap Stock Fraud Case
description: The SEC says a call center pushed 18 small-company stocks and generated more than $58 million in trading proceeds. Raymond Dove must pay about $4.6 million after a default judgment.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced October 8, 2026 that it has obtained final judgments against five defendants in an alleged microcap fraud. The case is SEC v. Francis Biller, et al., filed March 14, 2022.

According to the SEC’s complaint, Francis Biller, Chester Alvarez, Troy Gran-Brooks, Justin Plaizier and Raymond Dove ran a call center from at least January 2016 through at least July 2018. The SEC says the “boiler room” used high-pressure sales tactics to sell the stocks of small U.S. public companies to U.S. investors, including false or misleading statements about the callers’ own roles and about the companies. The SEC says the group promoted the stock of at least 18 issuers and generated more than $58 million in trading proceeds.

Judgments entered in early 2025 against Alvarez, Gran-Brooks, Plaizier and Biller permanently bar each from penny stock offerings. They were ordered to pay disgorgement plus prejudgment interest of $8,392,982 (Biller), $131,347 (Alvarez), $838,101 (Gran-Brooks) and $134,652 (Plaizier). The SEC says Alvarez, Gran-Brooks and Plaizier pleaded guilty and were sentenced in a parallel criminal case, and Biller has pleaded guilty and awaits sentencing.

On September 30, 2026 the court entered a default judgment against Dove. It ordered him to pay $2,923,446 in disgorgement and prejudgment interest and a civil penalty of $1,655,157, and barred him from participating in any penny stock offering. The court denied the SEC’s motion for default against relief defendant Shredderz International Corp. for lack of personal jurisdiction. The SEC says the litigation is now concluded.

sources.label: SEC: Francis Biller, et al., Litigation Release No. 26670 (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: SEC: SQN Capital and CEO Settle Charges, Receiver Appointed for Four Funds
description: The SEC says the New York adviser inflated fund values and missed audits for years. Jeremiah Silkowski agreed to a $200,000 penalty and an adviser bar.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced October 9, 2026 that New York-based investment adviser SQN Capital Management LLC and its president and majority owner, Jeremiah Silkowski, settled charges under the Investment Advisers Act. The SEC filed the case September 18, 2026 in the Southern District of New York, and the court entered consent judgments on October 8.

The SEC’s complaint alleges that from at least 2019 through 2025 the defendants breached their duties to four funds they managed. It says they did not have the funds’ annual financial statements audited, and that the only asset valuations were prepared by Silkowski alone, not by the independent valuation expert investors were told about. The SEC alleges he kept net asset values unchanged for years regardless of the assets’ performance, and repeatedly told investors without a reasonable basis that liquidation would soon be completed. The complaint says that left investors without access to their money.
The SEC also says SQN Capital was charged in 2020 and 2023 in settled administrative proceedings over failures to deliver audited financial statements, and that the conduct continued.

Neither defendant admitted or denied the allegations. Both consented to a court order appointing a receiver to liquidate the funds’ assets and distribute net proceeds to investors, and to permanent injunctions. Silkowski must pay a $200,000 civil penalty and is permanently barred from acting as or associating with an investment adviser, broker or dealer, except as the receiver needs his help.

sources.label: SEC: Jeremiah Silkowski and SQN Capital Management LLC, Litigation Release No. 26671 (Oct. 9, 2026)

title: SEC Charges Two Former Linqto Executives Over Pre-IPO Share Sales
description: The SEC says a Linqto subsidiary sold more than $430 million of pre-IPO vehicles to retail investors. It alleges prices were above fair value and “sold out” claims were false.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission charged William Sarris and Joseph Endoso, both former executives of San Jose, California-based Linqto, Inc., on October 9, 2026. The case was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. The charges are allegations, and the SEC seeks injunctions, disgorgement with interest, civil penalties and officer and director bars.

According to the SEC, a Linqto subsidiary sold more than $430 million of special purpose vehicles holding interests in private companies to retail investors from at least 2021 to 2024. The complaint says the executives misled investors in four ways: indicating prices reflected current market conditions or were below market when almost all offerings were priced above fair value; saying certain securities were “sold out” or “fully subscribed” when more shares were available; claiming an algorithm automatically set certain prices when Linqto staff still set them by hand; and touting compliance with securities laws after counsel had warned the business violated them.

The SEC also alleges the two unlawfully operated unregistered investment companies and sold securities in unregistered transactions to unaccredited investors. The complaint charges both under Section 17(a) of the Securities Act and Section 10(b) of the Exchange Act, plus Sections 5(a) and 5(c) of the Securities Act, and charges Sarris with control person liability.

sources.label: SEC: William Sarris and Joseph Endoso, Litigation Release No. 26672 (Oct. 9, 2026)

title: FTC: Premier Martial Arts Franchisor and Sales Firm to Pay $1.85 Million
description: The FTC says deceptive earnings claims drew more than 200 buyers to $49,500 franchises. Some franchisees would get the option to cancel without penalty.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Trade Commission announced October 5, 2026 that franchisor Premier Franchising Group LLC (PFG) and its former franchise sales organization, Franchise Fastlane LLC (FFL), will pay $1.85 million to settle allegations of misleading claims about the Premier Martial Arts (PMA) franchise and violations of the Franchise Rule. The settlements are proposed.

According to the FTC’s complaint, the companies claimed that people who were not martial artists could profitably run one or more PMA studios on a semi-absentee basis, working less than 15 hours a week. The FTC says those claims drew more than 200 consumers, including veterans, to pay PFG an initial franchise fee of $49,500 or more. It says they then spent hundreds of thousands of dollars more to build out and run studios, and many took on significant debt.

The complaint also alleges PFG made deceptive earnings claims in its 2020-2022 Franchise Disclosure Documents. The FTC says PFG reported significant income for existing studios without a reasonable basis to know whether that was representative of new studios. For example, many existing franchisees ran studios of 2,000 to 7,000 square feet, while PFG recommended new franchisees open 1,200 to 1,600 square feet.

Under the proposed settlement with PFG, certain franchisees will be able to cancel their franchise agreements without penalty. “Franchisors are legally required to be upfront and honest about earnings potential and the associated risks,” said Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection.

sources.label: FTC: Premier Martial Arts Franchisor and its Former Franchise Sales Organization Settle FTC Charges (Oct. 5, 2026)

title: FTC Closes Gildan and S&S Probe After Contract Change on Wholesale T-Shirt Pricing
description: The FTC says the partners amended an agreement that barred Gildan from offering S&S-level pricing to rival distributors. It cites the Robinson-Patman Act.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Trade Commission said October 8, 2026 that it secured changes to a partnership agreement between T-shirt maker Gildan Activewear SRL and wholesale distributor S&S Holdings LLC. The FTC says the changes protect small businesses and consumers from discriminatory pricing, and it has closed its investigation.

The FTC opened the probe after learning that S&S’s contract with Gildan prohibited Gildan from offering certain pricing and discounts given to S&S to S&S’s competitors. It examined whether Gildan violated Section 2(a) of the Robinson-Patman Act, which bars certain price discrimination, and whether S&S violated Section 2(f), which bars knowingly inducing or receiving prohibited price discrimination.

Gildan and S&S amended the agreement. It now says: “Nothing in this Agreement restricts or restrains Gildan’s discretion to set prices or offer partnership support to any other North American wholesale distributor.” The FTC posted a public letter from Gildan confirming the amendment.

The FTC said the matter builds on a Robinson-Patman settlement the prior week with Southern Glazer’s Wine and Spirits, which it described as the first such case resolved by a federal enforcement agency in over 20 years.

sources.label: FTC: FTC Secures Fair Pricing Protections by Taking Action Against Major Wholesale T-Shirt Distributors (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: SEC Seeks Final Judgment Against Ex-Western Asset CIO Ken Leech, $103 Million for Investors
description: Leech would pay a $3 million penalty and face an officer-and-director bar. With Western Asset’s $100 million penalty, the SEC says $103 million goes to harmed investors.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission said October 6, 2026 that it moved for a consent final judgment against Stephen Kenneth Leech II, former co-chief investment officer of Western Asset Management Company LLC. The SEC charged him in November 2024 with a multi-year cherry-picking allocation scheme.

The SEC alleges that from at least January 2021 through October 2023, Leech placed trades and then delayed allocations until near or after futures markets set daily settlement prices. That let him see price moves and steer hundreds of millions of dollars in first-day gains to favored portfolios and a similar amount of losses to disfavored ones.

Without admitting the allegations, Leech consented to a $3 million penalty, an officer-and-director bar and a permanent injunction against violating antifraud provisions, subject to court approval. He also agreed to a forthcoming associational bar. In June 2026 the SEC ordered Western Asset to pay a $100 million penalty and set up a Fair Fund for investors in the disfavored portfolios.

The SEC says the two resolutions together will return $103 million to harmed investors if the court approves. Leech pleaded guilty in June 2026 to obstruction of justice over false testimony to the SEC, with sentencing expected in the coming weeks.

sources.label: SEC: SEC Seeks Final Judgment Against Former Western Asset Co-CIO Ken Leech, Press Release 2026-103 (Oct. 6, 2026)

title: SEC Charges India-Based Man With Providing a Phony Audit Report to a U.S. Public Company
description: The SEC alleges Himanshu Jindal posed as a U.S. CPA and forged an engagement letter. The false report went into a Form 10-K that investors relied on.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced charges against Himanshu Jindal, also known as Manish Jindal, a citizen of India living in Jaipur, on October 6, 2026. The complaint was filed October 5 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia. The allegations have not been proven.

The SEC alleges Jindal had no accounting or auditing qualifications but told a freelance job platform he was a U.S. certified public accountant.
