Around August 2023 he answered a public company’s posting for a PCAOB-registered auditor, claiming to be a licensed CPA and PCAOB-registered auditor. The complaint says he supplied a fraudulent engagement letter purporting to come from a New York accounting firm, with a forged signature of its principal.

The SEC says he then provided a phony audit report that the company included in its annual report on Form 10-K, which investors relied on. He is charged with violating Section 10(b) of the Exchange Act and Rule 10b-5, and with aiding and abetting the issuer’s reporting violations. The SEC seeks injunctions, disgorgement with interest and a civil penalty.

sources.label: SEC: Himanshu Jindal a/k/a Manish Jindal, Litigation Release No. 26665 (Oct. 7, 2026)

title: SEC Charges Fintech Kalder and Founder Over Inflated Revenue in $6.7 Million Raise
description: The SEC alleges Kalder kept two sets of books and counted demo accounts as paying customers. Founder Gökçe Güven agreed to a bifurcated settlement.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced October 7, 2026 a partially settled action filed October 2 in the Southern District of New York against New York fintech Kalder Inc. and its founder and CEO, Gökçe Güven. The SEC says Kalder raised nearly $6.7 million from investors between about April and December 2024 using false statements about its financial performance.

According to the complaint, Kalder kept two sets of books: an accurate one prepared by its outside bookkeeper from third-party financial data, and a second with inflated figures created and sent to investors at Güven’s direction. The SEC says monthly revenue was far below what investors were shown, and that many customers described as in revenue-generating contracts had only signed up for free demo accounts or short-term discounted pilots.

Without admitting the allegations, Güven consented to a judgment, subject to court approval, that permanently enjoins her from violating the charged provisions and imposes a six-year officer-and-director bar. The court would set disgorgement with interest and civil penalties later. Güven previously pleaded guilty to securities fraud in a parallel criminal case.

sources.label: SEC: Kalder Inc. and Gökçe Güven, Litigation Release No. 26667 (Oct. 7, 2026)

title: 43 States Seek Approval of $400 Million Sandoz Generic Drug Price-Fixing Settlement
description: Washington’s attorney general says a coalition filed October 1 in Connecticut federal court. Consumers who bought generics from May 2009 to December 2019 may be eligible.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Washington Attorney General Nick Brown announced October 6, 2026 that he has joined a bipartisan coalition of 43 states and territories seeking court approval of a $400 million settlement with generic drug makers Sandoz Inc. and Fougera Pharmaceuticals Inc. The coalition filed a motion for preliminary approval on October 1 in U.S. District Court for the District of Connecticut.

The states allege the companies took part in long-running conspiracies to inflate and manipulate generic drug prices and reduce competition. The settlement also resolves allegations that Sandoz’s past and present international affiliates, including Novartis AG, Sandoz AG and Sandoz Group AG, took part and fraudulently transferred assets to avoid liability. Sandoz agreed to injunctive terms including internal reforms to ensure antitrust compliance. Washington’s share is more than $12 million.

Consumers who bought a generic prescription drug between May 2009 and December 2019 may be eligible for compensation. The state lists 1-866-290-0182, info@AGGenericDrugs.com and www.AGGenericDrugs.com for eligibility and claims. Washington and Idaho were the only states in the coalition to also secure restitution for businesses that indirectly bought the drugs or reimbursed their cost.
The Sandoz deal follows settlements with Glenmark, Lannett, Bausch, Apotex, and Heritage and its parent Emcure, totaling $96.5 million.

sources.label: Washington Attorney General: Washington, multistate coalition seek approval for $400 million settlement in drug price-fixing case (Oct. 6, 2026)

title: Nevada AG Urges Consumers to Claim Compensation for Inflated Generic Drug Prices
description: A federal court gave preliminary approval in late September to a plan to distribute about $96.5 million in settlement funds paid by generic drug makers.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford urged consumers on October 6, 2026 to check eligibility for compensation for certain generic drug purchases and file a claim online. He said that in late September the U.S. District Court for the District of Connecticut granted preliminary approval of a plan, filed by Nevada and a coalition of 47 other states and territories, to distribute settlement money paid by generic drug manufacturers.

The settlements, with Glenmark, Lannett, Bausch, Apotex, Heritage and Heritage’s parent Emcure, total about $96.5 million. They resolve claims that the companies illegally conspired to raise generic drug prices.

The states’ antitrust litigation began in 2016. The first complaint named Heritage, 17 other corporate defendants, two individuals and 15 generic drugs. A 2019 complaint named Teva and 21 other manufacturers and 16 executives. A third complaint, to be tried first, covers 80 topical generic drugs and names 26 corporate and 10 individual defendants. The states filed a fourth complaint earlier this year naming Novartis AG, Sandoz Group AG and Sandoz AG.

sources.label: Nevada Attorney General: Attorney General Ford Urges Consumers to Claim Compensation for Inflated Generic Drug Prices (Oct. 6, 2026)

title: Georgia AG Warns of Price Gouging and Scams Ahead of Hurricane Isaias
description: The state of emergency took effect October 8. Retailers may not raise prices on goods the governor designates, including motor fuel.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Georgia Attorney General Chris Carr warned Georgians on October 9, 2026 to watch for price gouging and scams tied to Hurricane Isaias. Governor Brian Kemp declared a state of emergency effective October 8, 2026. An earlier executive order on petroleum supply disruptions invoked the Price Gouging Statute starting September 29, 2026.

While the emergency lasts, businesses may not sell or offer to sell at retail any goods or services identified by the governor at a price higher than immediately before the declaration. Increases are allowed if they accurately reflect higher costs of new stock or transport plus the retailer’s average markup. The statute covers goods and services needed for preparation, response and recovery, including motor fuel, diesel and other petroleum products.

Georgians who suspect a scam or gouging can contact the Consumer Protection Division at 404-651-8600 or 1-800-869-1123, or use the online complaint form. Suspected contractor insurance fraud goes to the Insurance Commissioner at 404-656-2070 or 1-800-656-2298.

sources.label: Georgia Attorney General: Carr Warns Georgians of Price Gouging and Scams in Anticipation of Hurricane Isaias (Oct. 9, 2026)

title: North Carolina Wins Default Judgment Against Wedding Photography Company
description: The court ordered about $600,000 in restitution and more than $1.1 million in civil penalties. The AG says couples paid for photos and videos they never received.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: North Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson announced October 12, 2026 that a judge granted default judgment in his case against Holly Christina Photography and its owners, Holly Christina Scott Ayscue and Christopher Owen Ayscue. Judge Craig Croom ruled on Friday, October 9.

The office sued in February, alleging the defendants misled couples by failing to provide promised wedding photography and videography. The state received 228 consumer complaints about the company since January, with losses of nearly $600,000. In May a judge froze the defendants’ assets, ordered them to stop doing business in North Carolina and told them to deliver all photos and videos within 30 days. The state says they did not comply.

The judgment orders the defendants to turn over all raw and edited photos and videos consumers paid for, and to give the AG a list of the consumers who received them. It orders nearly $600,000 in restitution and more than $1.1 million in civil penalties. It also bars them from photography or videography contracts, from owning or running a business that takes advance deposits for those services, and from transferring assets derived from consumer payments.

sources.label: North Carolina Department of Justice: Attorney General Jeff Jackson Wins Wedding Photography Case; Judge Grants Default Judgment (Oct. 12, 2026)

title: New York AG Secures Up to $35 Million and Industry Ban From Ex-Celsius CEO Mashinsky
description: Letitia James says Alex Mashinsky misled more than 26,000 New York investors. He is permanently barred from securities, commodities and crypto.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: New York Attorney General Letitia James announced October 9, 2026 that she secured up to $35 million from Alex Mashinsky, co-founder and former CEO of crypto lending platform Celsius Network LLC, along with a permanent ban on his participation in the securities, commodities and cryptocurrency industries.

The office sued Mashinsky in 2023, alleging he misled hundreds of thousands of investors, including more than 26,000 in New York, about Celsius’s safety so they would deposit billions of dollars in digital assets. The office says Celsius lost hundreds of millions of dollars on risky investments, and that Mashinsky deceived investors about the platform’s safety, number of users and investment strategies, and repeatedly claimed it was safer than a bank. In fact, the office says, Celsius was not subject to the strict federal or state requirements banks face.

Mashinsky is serving a 12-year federal prison sentence under a plea agreement and was ordered to forfeit more than $48 million. The office says investors and creditors have received more than $3.4 billion in the Celsius bankruptcy proceeding.

sources.label: New York Attorney General: Attorney General James Bans Former Cryptocurrency CEO Who Defrauded Investors from Financial Industry (Oct. 9, 2026)

title: Former Nodus International Bank Chairman Sentenced to 62 Months for Looting the Bank
description: Juan Francisco Ramirez must forfeit about $13.6 million. DOJ says the scheme caused at least $23.6 million in losses and helped sink the Puerto Rican bank.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Justice Department announced October 7, 2026 that Juan Francisco Ramirez, 60, of Miami, former board chairman and co-owner of Nodus International Bank in Puerto Rico, was sentenced to 62 months in prison and three years of supervised release. He must forfeit about $13.6 million, the value of his proceeds. He pleaded guilty in September 2025 to conspiracy to commit wire fraud.

According to court documents, from 2017 to 2023 Ramirez and others invested more than $11 million of the bank’s funds in a Miami-based lender through sham investments so the money could be loaned to Ramirez and a co-conspirator. From 2018 to 2021 they induced the board and comptroller to buy at least 47 promissory notes totaling about $25.3 million from a finance company they jointly owned, and used the proceeds for personal investments, mortgages and credit card bills.

In March 2023 the Puerto Rico regulator, OCIF, told the bank it planned to place it in liquidation. On April 28, 2023, without OCIF authorization, Ramirez and a co-conspirator had the bank buy a roughly $26 million loan portfolio, mostly delinquent and uncollateralized, from their finance company to cover its debt. DOJ says the bank lost at least $23,613,371. IRS Criminal Investigation led the case.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Justice: Board Chairman and Co-Owner of Puerto Rican Bank Sentenced in Multimillion-Dollar Wire Fraud Conspiracy (Oct. 7, 2026)

title: Minnesota Woman Convicted in $3.6 Million Medicaid Housing Services Fraud
description: A federal jury found Sharmaine Meadows billed for services that were not provided. DOJ says the program shut down after costs ran 4,000 percent over estimates.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Justice Department announced October 8, 2026 that a federal jury in St. Paul convicted Sharmaine Meadows, 45, of Lake Elmo, Minnesota, of a scheme to steal $3.6 million from the now-defunct Minnesota Medicaid Housing Stabilization Services (HSS) Program.

Evidence at trial showed Meadows billed the program for housing services meant to move unhoused people into housing and help them keep it, without providing the services. The program allowed providers to bill up to 150 hours of transitional services and 150 hours of sustaining services per beneficiary. DOJ says Meadows told employees to maximize billings to the 150-hour cap even when the hours were not worked, and billed for in-person hours supposedly worked by employees who were in other states and countries, including the Philippines.
Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the National Fraud Enforcement Division said the program shut down entirely after its costs outran estimates by 4,000 percent.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Justice: Minnesota Woman Convicted in $3.6M Scheme to Defraud Medicaid Housing Services Program (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Federal Reserve Announces Enforcement Action Against American Express Over Money Laundering Controls
description: The Fed cites failures to detect and report suspicious activity. The OCC issued a separate action against the company’s national bank.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Reserve Board announced on October 8, 2026 an enforcement action against American Express Company to address, among other things, the firm’s failure to sufficiently detect and report certain suspicious activity related to money laundering.

The Board also identified significant deficiencies in how the firm’s enterprise-wide anti-money laundering program was implemented, in particular at its subsidiary national bank. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the national bank’s primary federal regulator, issued a separate enforcement action against the bank.
The Board said its action will help ensure the firm operates in compliance with all U.S. laws and regulations. The announcement did not state a dollar penalty in the release text.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board: Enforcement action against American Express Company (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Treasury Announces First Outbound Investment Program Penalty: $200,000 Against Amidi
description: Treasury says Amidi failed to notify it of a roughly $92,478 investment by a Chinese fund subsidiary in an AI robotics company.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Treasury Department announced October 7, 2026 that in July 2026 it issued its first civil penalty under the Outbound Investment Security Program (OISP). It penalized Amidi, LLC $200,000 for failing to submit a required notification of an investment by its controlled foreign entity into a Chinese embodied artificial intelligence company.

Treasury says that on April 19, 2025, Amidi’s subsidiary, a Chinese fund, invested about $92,478 in Shanghai Qiongche Intelligent Technology Company Limited (Noematrix), a private Chinese company developing AI, robotics and embodied intelligence. Amidi is also the parent of the organization that does business as Plug and Play Tech Center.

The OISP took effect January 2, 2025. It requires notification of certain investments, and prohibits others, by U.S. persons in entities connected to China, Hong Kong and Macau engaged in certain activities in quantum computing, artificial intelligence and related areas. Treasury said it found the transaction through its regular compliance and market monitoring. It also noted that Congress passed the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025 on December 18, 2025, which will expand the program to more countries and technology sectors.

sources.label: U.S. Treasury: Treasury Announces Enforcement Penalty for Violation of Outbound Program (Oct. 7, 2026)

title: Treasury: Do Not Pay Reaches 99% of Federal Programs, $3.7 Trillion in Payments Verified
description: Treasury says it screened more than 1.1 billion payments in fiscal 2026 and returned about 13,500 payments totaling $175 million that were headed to deceased people.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Treasury Department and the Bureau of the Fiscal Service reported on October 6, 2026 their fiscal year 2026 results on preventing fraud and improper payments. Treasury says about 99 percent of federal programs can now access all Do Not Pay data sources they are legally authorized to use, up from about 4 percent at the end of fiscal 2025.

Treasury screened more than 2.3 billion records against Do Not Pay data sources, up from 641 million in fiscal 2025, and added nine new datasets, including company registration data from OpenCorporates, select verification against Social Security’s Numident data and grantee audit findings from the Federal Audit Clearinghouse.

Under a new payment verification process, Treasury screened more than 1.1 billion federal payments totaling about $3.7 trillion. It says it identified and returned about 13,500 payments totaling $175 million that would have gone to deceased individuals. Capabilities to validate bank account ownership and the presence and format of Taxpayer Identification Numbers became fully operational September 30, 2026.

sources.label: U.S. Treasury: Treasury Reports Major Progress in Preventing Fraud and Improper Payments (Oct. 6, 2026)

title: Florida Marketer Convicted in COVID-19 Testing Scheme That Billed Medicare Over $15 Million
description: Prosecutors say seniors at West Palm Beach-area clubs got tests they did not want. Medicare paid more than $500,000.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Justice Department announced October 7, 2026 that a federal jury in the Southern District of Florida convicted Joseph Rodriguez, 58, of Coral Springs, a laboratory vice president who ran a marketing company, Phoenix Health, of conspiracy to commit health care fraud and six counts of health care fraud.

According to court documents and trial evidence, Rodriguez organized drive-through COVID-19 testing events at residence country clubs in the West Palm Beach area. Elderly patients who signed up for nasal swab and antibody tests were also subjected to tens or even hundreds of unnecessary blood tests, from hormone tests to heavy metal panels, that no doctor ordered. Those were billed to Medicare as medically necessary, with a doctor’s name fraudulently listed on the claims.

The claims covered tests at nine clubs over about four months involving almost 2,000 patients. Medicare was billed more than $15 million and paid over $500,000. Each count carries a maximum of 10 years in prison, and sentencing is expected in January 2027.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Justice: Florida Laboratory Vice President and Marketer Convicted of Medicare Fraud for COVID-19 Testing Scheme (Oct. 7, 2026)

title: SEC Charges Former Pharma HR Executive With Insider Trading Ahead of Adamas Deal
description: The SEC alleges Mukesh Asudani and two other accounts made about $78,751 after the Supernus-Adamas announcement. Adamas stock rose about 75%.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced charges on September 30, 2026 against Mukesh Asudani, a former senior vice president of human resources at a publicly traded pharmaceutical company, for alleged insider trading ahead of the October 11, 2021 announcement that Supernus Pharmaceuticals agreed to acquire Adamas Pharmaceuticals. Asudani lives in India. The SEC’s release refers to his former employer as “Pharma Company A.”

The complaint says Asudani joined internal meetings remotely and learned that his employer was bidding for Adamas. On October 4, 2021, the day the board met and the company submitted its best and final offer, he allegedly sold his entire position in his employer’s stock and used the proceeds and nearly all the cash in his brokerage account to buy Adamas shares. He also allegedly had two other brokerage accounts, one his son’s and one a family friend’s, buy Adamas shares that day.

After the announcement Adamas stock rose about 75%, and the SEC says the three accounts together made about $78,751 in illicit profits. The complaint, filed in the Southern District of New York, charges violations of Sections 10(b) and 14(e) of the Exchange Act. The SEC seeks an injunction, disgorgement with interest, a civil penalty and an officer-and-director bar.

sources.label: SEC: Mukesh Asudani, Litigation Release No. 26662 (Sept. 30, 2026)

title: SEC Charges Mississippi Man Over $1.94 Million in Medical Marijuana Investor Funds
description: The SEC alleges Thomas Moore raised about $4.94 million for Mississippi Green Oil and spent $1.94 million on personal items such as jewelry and travel.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced October 1, 2026 that it charged Thomas J. Moore, III, of D’Iberville, Mississippi, with misappropriating about $1.94 million from about 20 individuals in connection with a medical marijuana business he primarily owned and controlled. The complaint was filed September 30 in the Southern District of Mississippi.

According to the SEC, between at least December 2021 and August 2024 Moore raised about $4.94 million from investors who bought equity interests in Mississippi Green Oil, LLC, a Prentiss, Mississippi company he set up around December 2020. He told investors the money would develop the business. The SEC says he spent about $1.94 million on personal expenses unrelated to the company, including jewelry and travel.

The complaint also alleges Moore promised short-term profit distributions but paid none, and did not disclose related lawsuits by other investors alleging that principal was not returned and promised distributions were not paid. He is charged under Section 17(a) of the Securities Act and Section 10(b) of the Exchange Act. The SEC seeks injunctions, disgorgement with interest and a civil penalty.

sources.label: SEC: Thomas J. Moore, III, Litigation Release No. 26663 (Oct. 1, 2026)

title: SEC Charges Former Global Tech Industries CEO Over Share Issuances “For Services”
description: The SEC alleges David Reichman issued tens of millions of shares to family and associates who provided no services, and hid his daughter’s large holding.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced October 2, 2026 that it filed charges against David Reichman, former chairman and CEO of Global Tech Industries Group, Inc., for allegedly running a multi-year scheme to defraud investors. The complaint, filed in the Southern District of New York, also names his daughter, Justine Reichman, individually and as trustee of the Justine Reichman 2021 Trust, as relief defendants.

The SEC alleges Reichman caused Global Tech to issue tens of millions of shares to family members, friends and associates to enrich himself and his daughter. It says he signed annual filings stating the shares were issued “for services,” knowing the recipients had provided none, concealed that his daughter was a significant shareholder, and failed to file required reports on his own stock sales on time.

He is charged with violating Section 17(a) of the Securities Act, Section 10(b) of the Exchange Act and Rule 10b-5, and the Section 16(a) reporting rules, and with aiding and abetting the company’s reporting violations. The SEC seeks injunctions, civil penalties, disgorgement with interest and an officer-and-director bar, and disgorgement from the relief defendants.

sources.label: SEC: David Reichman et al., Litigation Release No. 26664 (Oct. 2, 2026)

title: SEC Charges Encinitas Investment Adviser in Alleged Cherry-Picking Scheme
description: The SEC says Darren Caris steered profitable trades to his own account and losing trades to clients from December 2023 to April 2024.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced on October 8, 2026 charges against Darren J. Caris and his firm, Caris Investment Partners, Inc., of Encinitas, California, for allegedly defrauding clients through a cherry-picking scheme and related false statements. The complaint was filed October 6 in the Southern District of California.

According to the SEC, from December 2023 to April 2024 Caris placed trades through the firm’s block trading account and later in the day disproportionately allocated profitable trades to his personal account and unprofitable trades to some clients’ accounts. The SEC also alleges he and the firm made false and misleading statements to clients and prospects about how trades were allocated, how his personal trading conflicts were managed, and the firm’s move to a different broker-dealer custodian.

They are charged under Section 17(a) of the Securities Act, Section 10(b) of the Exchange Act and Rule 10b-5, and Sections 206(1) and 206(2) of the Advisers Act. The SEC seeks injunctions, disgorgement with interest and civil penalties. The charges are allegations.

sources.label: SEC: Darren J. Caris and Caris Investment Partners, Inc., Litigation Release No. 26669 (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: SEC Obtains Judgments Totaling About $5.7 Million Against Three BitConnect Promoters
description: Courts ordered Michael Noble, Craig Grant and Trevon Brown to pay disgorgement, interest and penalties over the BitConnect “lending program.”
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced September 30, 2026 that it obtained final judgments against three promoters of BitConnect’s “lending program”: Michael Noble, Craig Grant and Trevon Brown. The SEC’s complaint, filed May 28, 2021 in the Southern District of New York, alleged they offered and sold unregistered securities from about June 2017 to January 2018 without being registered as broker-dealers.

On July 17, 2026 the court ordered Noble to pay $731,281 in disgorgement, $293,703.36 in prejudgment interest and a $50,000 penalty, $1,074,984.36 in total. On August 7, 2026 it entered a default judgment against Grant for $1,748,147 in disgorgement, $702,105.84 in interest and a $230,480 penalty, $2,680,732.84 in total. On September 9, 2026 it entered a consent judgment against Brown for $1,728,563 in disgorgement, $182,902.15 in interest and a $75,000 penalty, $1,986,465.15 in total.
The judgments also permanently enjoin each man from violating registration provisions of the securities laws and bar them from participating in a digital asset securities offering.

sources.label: SEC: Trevon Brown, Craig Grant, and Michael Noble, Litigation Release No. 26660 (Sept. 30, 2026)

title: SEC Settles With Ex-GigaMedia Access CEO and Executive in $37 Million Investor Fraud Case
description: Robert Bernardi agreed to disgorgement of $4.7 million plus interest, deemed satisfied by criminal restitution. The SEC says Sunil Chandra posed as a customer employee.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission said on September 30, 2026 it filed consents and proposed final judgments against Robert Bernardi, founder and former CEO of private software company GigaMedia Access Corporation, and Sunil Chandra, its former vice president of international business development. The SEC sued in October 2021 in the Southern District of New York.

The SEC alleged that between March 2018 and August 2019 Bernardi raised more than $37 million from investors while repeatedly misrepresenting the company’s financial condition. When an investor asked to speak with a customer, Bernardi allegedly arranged for Chandra to pretend to be an employee of a company Bernardi claimed was a customer.

Subject to court approval, Bernardi would be permanently enjoined from violating antifraud provisions and liable for $4,700,000 in disgorgement and $670,173.72 in prejudgment interest. Chandra would be enjoined and liable for $50,000 plus $4,094.83 in interest. Both amounts are deemed satisfied by restitution orders in the parallel criminal cases.

sources.label: SEC: Robert Bernardi and Sunil Chandra, Litigation Release No. 26661 (Sept. 30, 2026)

title: FTC Settles With Southern Glazer’s Over Wine and Spirits Price Discrimination
description: The order covers nearly all Southern sales to the five largest chain retailers in 26 states, with cash payments to small businesses if a monitor finds a violation.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Trade Commission announced October 2, 2026 a settlement with Southern Glazer’s Wine and Spirits LLC, the nation’s largest wine and spirits distributor, over alleged price discrimination. The FTC called it the successful conclusion of its first Robinson-Patman Act enforcement action in a generation.

The FTC sued in 2024, alleging Southern charged independent retailers significantly higher prices than large chains such as Total Wine, Walmart and Kroger for identical bottles in the same period, even when stores were a few blocks apart. It alleged the gap came from discounts and rebates large buyers could get and small competitors could not, not justified by differences in distribution cost.

Under the proposed stipulated order, Southern will face limits on charging small, independent retailers higher prices than competing large chains. The settlement covers nearly all of Southern’s wine and spirits sales to the five largest chain retailers in 26 states. It also provides direct cash payments to harmed small businesses if an independent monitor finds Southern violates the order.

sources.label: FTC: FTC Secures Settlement that Protects Small Businesses from Illegal Price Discrimination (Oct. 2, 2026)

title: FTC and USDA Seek Public Comment on Farm Equipment Markets, Comments Due December 7
description: The joint inquiry asks farmers and repair providers about barriers to buying and servicing agricultural equipment.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Trade Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture launched a joint public inquiry on October 7, 2026 into agricultural equipment manufacturing and distribution markets, including potential anticompetitive conduct. They said USDA has received a growing number of complaints that farmers face barriers to acquiring equipment and the services needed to keep it running.

The agencies invite comments from farmers, independent repair providers and current and former employees of equipment makers and dealers. Topics include business models, policies and contract terms; firsthand experiences or documented cases of restrictions, penalties or retaliation; and effects on pricing, market entry, innovation and farmer welfare.

Comments go through Regulations.gov and must arrive by 11:59 p.m. on December 7, 2026. The FTC noted its recent settlements involving Corteva in pesticides markets, joined by twelve states, and Deere & Company over repair restrictions, joined by five states.

sources.label: FTC: FTC and USDA Seek Public Comment on Agricultural Equipment Manufacturing and Distribution Market Practices (Oct. 7, 2026)

title: FTC Warns 24 Large Healthcare Companies That Hidden Prices Can Be Deceptive
description: Chairman Andrew Ferguson’s letters say meeting CMS price transparency rules does not create a safe harbor under the FTC Act.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: FTC Chairman Andrew N. Ferguson sent letters on October 5, 2026 to 24 of the nation’s largest healthcare services companies, reminding them of their obligation to give patients timely, accurate and complete pricing information. The FTC said failing to do so can be an unfair or deceptive practice under Section 5 of the FTC Act.

The letters focus on routine, non-emergency care scheduled in advance. They say compliance with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services price transparency rules is a baseline, not a safe harbor from FTC Act liability. Because price is a material term, clear and conspicuous disclosure is often needed. An omission can mislead, and a disclosure can still be deceptive if incomplete, such as leaving out physician or facility fees or covering only part of the expected care.

The FTC also says unclear or late pricing may be unfair if it causes substantial injury consumers cannot reasonably avoid, because patients cannot comparison shop. The FTC described the letters as part of its work on healthcare affordability and price transparency.

sources.label: FTC: FTC Issues Letters Warning Hospitals Against Deceptive Pricing Practices (Oct. 5, 2026)

title: Pacearth Recalls About 110,550 Swing Seats Sold on Amazon After Fall Injuries
description: CPSC says seats, carabiners or straps can break. Pacearth has received at least 30 fall reports with nine injuries, and offers a full refund.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced on October 8, 2026 that Pacearth Direct, of City of Industry, California, is recalling about 110,550 PACEARTH U-type swing seats. The seats, metal carabiners or quick links, or webbing straps can break during use, posing a fall hazard.

The seats came in green, blue, pink, red and turquoise, with a chain coated in yellow plastic, and were sold singly or in two-packs. They were sold on Amazon.com from May 2017 through June 2026 for between $27 and $57. Pacearth has received at least 30 reports of falls with at least nine injuries, including fractures, head injuries and bruising.

Consumers should stop using the swing seats immediately. For a full refund, write “RECALLED” on the seat with permanent marker, take a photo that shows the PACEARTH logo and email it to recall@pacearth.com. The CPSC recall number is 27-019.

sources.label: CPSC: Pacearth Direct Recalls PACEARTH Swing Seats Due to Risk of Serious Injury from Fall Hazard (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Iowa Unclaimed Property Program Passes $450 Million Returned
description: State Treasurer Roby Smith says the program returned a record $38.2 million in fiscal 2026. A new Money Match tool returns some property without a claim.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Iowa State Treasurer Roby Smith announced on October 7, 2026 that the Great Iowa Treasure Hunt has surpassed $450 million returned to current and former Iowans since it began. In fiscal year 2026 it returned a record $38.2 million and paid a record 53,194 claims, 8,302 more than the year before.

Unclaimed property can include forgotten checking and savings accounts, uncashed checks, utility refunds, stocks, life insurance proceeds and the contents of abandoned safe deposit boxes. The Treasurer’s office holds it until the owner or heir claims it. The office says one in seven Iowans has funds in the program.

In 2026 the Treasurer launched Money Match, which automatically returns certain qualifying properties without a claim. Not all properties qualify, so the office urges people to search their name, previous names, previous addresses, businesses and family members at GreatIowaTreasureHunt.gov.

sources.label: Iowa State Treasurer: Treasurer Smith Announces $450 Million Returned Through Great Iowa Treasure Hunt (Oct. 7, 2026)

title: FDA Updates Salmonella Outbreak Investigation Tied to Recalled Broccoli Sprouting Seeds
description: The FDA says not to use recalled lots from Gardeners Basics, Eden Brothers and Home Grown. The investigation is ongoing.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Food and Drug Administration updated its Salmonella outbreak investigation involving sprouts on October 9, 2026. It says consumers, restaurants and retailers should not use recalled lots of broccoli seeds, and that its investigation is ongoing.

Recalled products include Gardeners Basics Waltham 29 Broccoli Sprouting Seeds in one-pound bags (UPC 848137042889, marked “Packed for 2027”), sold nationwide on Amazon, gardenersbasics.com, TikTok Shop, Walmart, eBay and Etsy. Also recalled are Eden Brothers calabrese broccoli seeds, lots 1022067 and 1022068, sold on Edenbrothers.com and Amazon from July 8 to September 28, 2026, and Home Grown green sprouting calabrese broccoli seeds, 8 oz, lot code AUG172026, sold on Amazon from August 20 to September 18, 2026. Recalled Evergreen Fresh Sprouts, LLC broccoli sprouts are past expiration and no longer on sale.

Salmonella illness usually starts 12 to 72 hours after eating contaminated food and lasts four to seven days, with diarrhea, fever and abdominal cramps. Children under five, older adults and people with weakened immune systems are more likely to have severe infections. The FDA advises cleaning and sanitizing surfaces and containers that touched recalled products and contacting a health care provider if symptoms appear.

sources.label: FDA: Outbreak Investigation of Salmonella: Sprouts (September 2026), updated Oct. 9, 2026

title: CMS Publishes 2027 Medicare Advantage and Part D Star Ratings Ahead of Open Enrollment
description: CMS says about 37% of MA-PD contracts earned four stars or higher. Open enrollment runs October 15 to December 7, 2026.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services published the 2027 Medicare Advantage and Part D Star Ratings on October 8, 2026 on Medicare Plan Finder. Open enrollment for 2027 coverage begins October 15, 2026 and runs through December 7, 2026. The ratings also affect 2028 MA quality bonus payments.

CMS says about 37% of Medicare Advantage prescription drug (MA-PD) contracts offered in 2027, or 188 contracts, earned four stars or higher. Weighted by enrollment, about 71% of MA-PD enrollees are in contracts with four or more stars in 2027. MA-PD contracts are rated on up to 43 measures, MA-only contracts on up to 32 and standalone Part D plans on up to 13.

CMS added two new measures, Concurrent Use of Opioids and Benzodiazepines and Polypharmacy: Use of Multiple Anticholinergic Medications in Older Adults. It retired the Care for Older Adults Pain Assessment and Medication Reconciliation Post-Discharge measures. CMS says year-over-year rating changes are normal because cut points are recalculated annually.

sources.label: CMS: 2027 Medicare Advantage and Part D Star Ratings fact sheet (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: New York AG Indicts Queens Pharmacy Owner Over Alleged $31 Million Medicaid and ADAP Fraud
description: Letitia James says Miguel Baron paid cash kickbacks and billed for medications never dispensed. A civil forfeiture action seeks over $95 million.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: New York Attorney General Letitia James announced October 7, 2026 the arrest and indictment of Miguel Baron, 62, of Yonkers, who owns two Jackson Heights pharmacies, Guardiola Pharmacy and Baron Specialty Pharmacy. The office alleges he directed a scheme that stole more than $31 million from Medicaid and the AIDS Drug Assistance Program (ADAP) and endangered New Yorkers with HIV. The charges are allegations.

The Medicaid Fraud Control Unit says that from January 1, 2023 to April 29, 2026, Baron and co-conspirators encouraged Medicaid recipients to fill prescriptions at his pharmacies by paying them cash kickbacks. The office says the pharmacies billed Medicaid and ADAP for medications that were never dispensed to patients.

The attorney general also filed a civil asset forfeiture action to seize and place liens on assets bought with the alleged proceeds, including luxury properties in Miami, a Mercedes-Benz, a Lexus and tickets to the 2026 FIFA World Cup in Miami. The action seeks over $95 million in damages.

sources.label: New York Attorney General: Attorney General James Announces Arrest and Indictment of Queens Pharmacy Owner for Stealing More Than $31 Million (Oct. 7, 2026)

title: OCC Lets National Banks Close Offices in Areas Hit by Hurricane Isaias
description: The proclamation covers affected areas of Alabama and Mississippi. The OCC expects only directly affected offices to close and reopen quickly.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued a proclamation on October 8, 2026 allowing national banks, federal savings associations, and federal branches and agencies of foreign banks to close offices in areas of Alabama and Mississippi affected by Hurricane Isaias. The release headline also lists Florida.

The OCC said it expects only bank offices directly affected by potentially unsafe conditions to close, and that those offices should make every effort to reopen as quickly as possible to meet customers’ banking needs.

The agency pointed banks to OCC Bulletin 2012-28, “Supervisory Guidance on Natural Disasters and Other Emergency Conditions,” which describes steps banks can consider when they operate or have customers in disaster areas. Customers of affected banks should check with their bank for branch status.

sources.label: OCC: News Release 2026-88, OCC Allows National Banks and Federal Savings Associations in Alabama, Florida, and Mississippi Affected by Hurricane Isaias to Close (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Treasury’s OFAC Removes 125 Names From Sanctions Lists in Third Modernization Round
description: OFAC also updated 22 entries to improve compliance screening. Removed entries include deceased people, defunct companies and entries lacking identifying information.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Treasury Department said on October 5, 2026 that its Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) removed 125 individuals and entities from its sanctions lists and updated 22 list entries to improve compliance screening. It is the third round of the sanctions modernization effort Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced in May.

Treasury says those removed include deceased individuals, defunct companies and entries lacking enough information for reliable compliance screening. It says OFAC conducted an interagency review to ensure the removals would not harm U.S. foreign policy or national security interests.

Treasury said the goal is for sanctions to stay targeted, effective and aligned with U.S. economic, foreign policy and national security priorities, and that the administration measures sanctions by effect and impact, not the number of names listed.

sources.label: U.S. Treasury: Treasury Announces Third Round of Sanctions Removals, Updates in Modernization Initiative (Oct. 5, 2026)

title: DOJ Fraud Division Directive 26-13 Calls for Early Asset Seizures and Infrastructure Takedowns
description: Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald’s memo tells prosecutors to use tax, securities, consumer fraud and cyber authorities together.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division released Directive 26-13 on October 8, 2026, outlining the division’s approach to investigating, disrupting and prosecuting fraud. It builds on earlier guidance on the division’s priorities and corporate enforcement policy.

The Justice Department calls it a significant operational shift. It requires prosecutors to attack fraud from all angles using the division’s tax, securities fraud, consumer fraud and cybercrime authorities, and to use early, pre-indictment asset seizures and digital-infrastructure takedowns to halt schemes and freeze assets in real time.

The directive also urges prosecutors to develop cooperators, vigorously prosecute corporate bad actors, seek arrest and detention in appropriate cases and advocate fully at sentencing. DOJ says the goal is to disrupt and dismantle fraudulent networks before they cause widespread harm.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Justice: Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald Issues Memorandum on the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Comprehensive Approach in the Fight Against Fraud (Oct. 8, 2026)

title: FTC, Utah and Nevada Sue Lens.com Over Hidden “Taxes & Fees” on Contact Lenses
description: The complaint alleges a mandatory charge buried at checkout often doubles the advertised price. Lens.com’s AutoRefill plan is also challenged.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Federal Trade Commission, joined by the Utah and Nevada attorneys general, sued contact lens retailer Lens.com Inc. on October 2, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Nevada. The complaint also names owner Cary Samourkachian and affiliate Speed Commerce LLC. The FTC voted 2-0 to file, and the court will decide the case.

The complaint alleges Lens.com advertises low prices in sponsored Google search ads and on its website, then adds a mandatory “Taxes & fees” charge at checkout that routinely doubles the price and costs consumers hundreds of millions of dollars. It says the line item sits below the visible part of the screen while a prominent “Continue” button encourages shoppers to proceed, so many never see it. It also says the label suggests state sales tax, although many states exempt contact lenses from sales tax or have none.

The complaint further alleges the same low prices lure shoppers into the AutoRefill subscription without clear disclosure of the charge, and that Lens.com buries how and by when to cancel to avoid a future shipment. The plaintiffs allege violations of the FTC Act, the Restore Online Shoppers’ Confidence Act, the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act and Utah and Nevada consumer laws.

sources.label: FTC: FTC, States Sue Lens.com for Misrepresenting the Price of Contact Lenses in Search Ads and on Its Website (Oct. 2, 2026)

title: White House Says Nearly 70 Million Trump Accounts Created, Parents Must Claim Them
description: The administration reports $4.5 billion deposited since July 4. Family contributions are capped at $5,000 a year and employer contributions at $2,500.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The White House said on October 7, 2026 that nearly 70 million Trump Accounts, tax-advantaged investment accounts for children, have been created, including more than 60 million through automatic enrollment. It says every child under 18 with a Social Security number now has an account in their name. These figures are the administration’s own.

Parents or guardians must claim an account through the Trump Accounts App to manage it, allow contributions from family and friends and receive the one-time $1,000 seed contribution for eligible children. The White House says more than $4.5 billion has been deposited since the July 4 launch: $1.3 billion in seed contributions, over $600 million from family and friends, and $2.6 billion in philanthropic gifts.

Family and friends can contribute up to $5,000 per year. Employers can contribute up to $2,500 per year, within the overall $5,000 limit. The White House says an estimated 80% of accounts are linked to families earning under $200,000 a year, and that more than 70 companies have committed to contributions for employees.

sources.label: The White House: Trump Accounts Put 70 Million Kids on the Path to Financial Freedom (Oct. 7, 2026)

title: Pennsylvania AG Settles With Mavis Tire for $215,000 Over Alleged Unnecessary Repairs
description: Consumers who believe they were billed for services they did not need have until January 26, 2027 to file a complaint for restitution.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday announced a settlement on September 28, 2026 with Mavis Tire Supply, LLC over allegedly deceptive sales practices. Mavis will pay $215,000 in monetary relief, with another $100,000 due if it violates the settlement. Mavis operates more than 130 branches in Pennsylvania and agreed to maintain oversight and training to ensure employees comply with the law.

The settlement, an Assurance of Voluntary Compliance filed in Philadelphia County Court of Common Pleas, resolves an investigation into allegations that Mavis recommended and charged for repair and maintenance services that were unnecessary or never performed, and failed to perform work in a skilled, workmanlike manner. A settlement is not an admission of a violation.

It includes $190,000 in restitution for harmed consumers who have filed or file a complaint with sufficient support by Tuesday, January 26, 2027, and $25,000 for costs. Affected customers can file with the Bureau of Consumer Protection online, at 1-800-441-2555 or at scams@attorneygeneral.gov.

sources.label: Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General: Bureau of Consumer Protection Secures Settlement with Mavis Discount Tire Regarding Billing for Unnecessary Services (Sept. 28, 2026)

title: CVS Agrees to Pay $315 Million Over Opioid Prescriptions and False Claims, DOJ Says
description: The settlement covers October 2013 through December 2025. CVS must add safeguards, including monitoring of opioid prescribing patterns.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Justice Department announced October 13, 2026 that CVS Pharmacy Inc. and related entities agreed to pay $315 million to resolve allegations that from October 17, 2013 through December 2, 2025 they illegally filled opioid and other controlled-substance prescriptions in violation of the Controlled Substances Act, then sought payment for many of them from Medicare and other federal health programs in violation of the False Claims Act.

The government filed its complaint December 13, 2024 in the District of Rhode Island, alleging CVS knowingly filled prescriptions that lacked a legitimate medical purpose or were not valid. The case began as a whistleblower suit by former CVS employee Hillary Estright, which the United States took over. Her share of the recovery has not been set.

Under the agreement CVS must put in place additional safeguards so opioids and other controlled substances are dispensed only when medically appropriate, including proactive monitoring of opioid prescribing patterns. The settlement resolves allegations; it is not a finding of liability.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Justice: CVS Agrees to Pay $315M for Illegally Filling Unlawful Opioid Prescriptions and for Submitting False Claims to the Federal Government (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: DOJ: “Joint Disruption Week” Hits West African Scam Networks, 3.7 Million Accounts Removed
description: Law enforcement made 28 arrests in Ghana and Nigeria. Private partners say they flagged over $11 million in potentially freezable funds.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Justice Department announced October 13, 2026 results of a “Joint Disruption Week” the week of October 6 targeting online scam accounts and transnational criminal networks in West Africa. It called it the first coordinated effort focused on the region, hosted by the UK National Crime Agency with U.S. and African law enforcement and private companies.

Companies including Meta, Google, Microsoft, Coinbase, Binance and Chainalysis took action on their own networks. They told DOJ they removed more than 3.7 million accounts, Pages and Groups targeting people in the U.S., UK and elsewhere, shared leads on more than 30 suspected scam centers, and identified over $11 million in potentially freezable funds.

Authorities made 28 arrests. In Ghana, officials arrested 19 people in the Accra suburb of Sasaabi and seized 303 devices; they identified 117 human trafficking victims awaiting repatriation to Nigeria and 89 scam victims with approximate losses of $8.3 million. In Nigeria, nine people were arrested and 53 devices seized. DOJ says the disrupted schemes included law enforcement impersonation scams and digital “arrest” extortion.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Justice: The Department of Justice Announces Results of Law Enforcement and Private Industry Joint Disruption Week Targeting Online Scam Accounts and Transnational Criminal Networks Operating in West Africa (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: Cape Cod Man Pleads Guilty to Laundering Proceeds of $6 Million Medicare Equipment Fraud
description: DOJ says Advanced Medical Supply billed Medicare for braces patients never ordered. Beneficiaries mailed boxes back with notes calling it a scam.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Justice Department announced October 13, 2026 that Leo Anzivino Jr., 35, of Falmouth, Massachusetts, pleaded guilty to conspiring to launder proceeds of a health care fraud scheme of more than $6 million. He agreed to be the nominal owner of Advanced Medical Supply Corp. of Rochester, New Hampshire, though co-conspirators actually owned and ran it.

According to court documents, Advanced billed Medicare more than $6 million for durable medical equipment such as knee and back braces that beneficiaries did not need and doctors did not prescribe, using fake physician orders. Medicare paid more than $3 million. DOJ says beneficiaries returned boxes with notes saying they had not ordered the items and calling it a scam.

Anzivino was listed as owner on Medicare enrollment papers and gave a bank false ownership certifications. After learning Medicare billing privileges would be revoked, he wired $1,494,938.09 in three transfers over about five weeks. The government seized about $353,768 from Advanced’s account in 2024. Sentencing is January 21, 2027, with a maximum of 10 years.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Justice: Cape Cod Man Pleads Guilty to Conspiring to Launder Proceeds of $6M Medicare Fraud Scheme (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: Pennsylvania AG Sues Insulin Makers and PBMs Over Alleged Price Manipulation
description: The complaint names Eli Lilly, Novo Nordisk, Sanofi, Express Scripts, CVS Caremark and Optum Rx. It seeks restitution for Pennsylvanians.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday announced October 13, 2026 that his Antitrust Section filed a complaint in Commonwealth Court against drugmakers and pharmacy benefit managers over alleged collusion to manipulate insulin prices and raise patients’ out-of-pocket costs. The claims are allegations.

Defendants include Eli Lilly and Company, Novo Nordisk Inc. and Sanofi-Aventis US LLC, and numerous PBMs including Express Scripts, CVS Caremark and Optum Rx. The complaint alleges violations of Pennsylvania’s Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law, plus unjust enrichment and civil conspiracy, and alleges the parties conspired to inflate insulin prices by more than 1,000 percent.

The office says about 1.3 million Pennsylvanians have diabetes and 3.5 million more have prediabetes, and that diagnosed diabetes costs the state an estimated $16.4 billion a year. The complaint seeks structural changes to bring costs down to fair market prices and give patients options, restitution for people harmed, civil penalties and costs.

sources.label: Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General: AG Sunday’s Antitrust Section Takes Action Against Insulin Makers, PBMs for Pricing Scheme (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: Tennessee Joins 45-State Generic Drug Settlements With Ascend, Citron and Mayne
description: Ascend would pay $400,000 and Mayne $650,000. The states’ first trial is set for February 2027 in Hartford.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Tennessee Attorney General Jonathan Skrmetti announced October 13, 2026 that Tennessee joined a coalition of 45 states and territories seeking court approval of settlements with generic drug makers Ascend Laboratories, Citron Pharma and Mayne Pharma. The settlements resolve allegations of a conspiracy to inflate prices, reduce competition and restrain trade in generic prescription drugs.

Ascend will pay $400,000 and Mayne $650,000. Citron’s settlement carries injunctive terms that apply if it re-enters the generic drug business. All three agreed to internal reforms to promote antitrust compliance. Earlier settlements with Sandoz, Glenmark, Lannett, Bausch, Apotex, and Heritage and its parent Emcure total $496.5 million, per the release.

Consumers who bought certain generic prescription drugs in the U.S. between May 2009 and December 2019 may be eligible for compensation. They can call 1-866-290-0182, email info@AGGenericDrugs.com or visit www.AGGenericDrugs.com. The states are preparing for the first trial in February 2027 in Hartford, Connecticut.

sources.label: Tennessee Attorney General: Attorney General Skrmetti Announces Settlements with Generic Drug Manufacturers (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: OFAC Settles With Freight Forwarder Pegasus Worldwide Logistics for $175,015
description: Treasury says Pegasus dealt in blocked property and took six months to fully answer an OFAC subpoena. OFAC called the conduct non-egregious.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control announced October 9, 2026 a $175,015 settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, a freight forwarding firm in cross-border shipments. The amount settles potential civil liability for four apparent violations of the Illicit Drug Trafficking Sanctions Regulations and six apparent violations of the Reporting, Procedures and Penalties Regulations.

OFAC says that between September 2023 and February 2024 Pegasus dealt in blocked property by facilitating the importation of a machine supplied by a designated company, and failed to fully respond to an OFAC subpoena for six months. OFAC determined the conduct was non-egregious and not voluntarily disclosed, which shaped the amount.

The same OFAC notice issued International Criminal Court-related General Licenses 13 through 16 and made list changes, including adding the International Criminal Court to the SDN List and removing one Burma-related individual.

sources.label: U.S. Treasury OFAC: Recent Actions, Pegasus Worldwide Logistics settlement (Oct. 9, 2026)

title: Il Fornaio to Pay $3 Million to Settle EEOC Sexual Harassment Suit
description: The EEOC says at least 100 women, many of them teenagers, were affected across the chain’s California and Nevada restaurants.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission announced October 13, 2026 that Il Fornaio (America) LLC, an Italian restaurant chain with 15 locations in California and Nevada, will pay $3 million and provide other relief to settle a sexual harassment and retaliation lawsuit on behalf of a class of female employees.

The EEOC’s suit alleged supervisors and employees at its restaurants repeatedly sexually harassed female employees, many of them teenagers, including groping and requests for sexual favors. It alleged the women complained, the company did not stop the harassment and retaliated against many, and several resigned. The EEOC says it learned of at least 100 women affected.

The agency says the conduct violates Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. It filed EEOC v. Il Fornaio (America) LLC, No. 2:22-cv-05992, in the Central District of California after conciliation failed. Workers who face harassment or retaliation can file a charge with the EEOC.

sources.label: U.S. EEOC: Il Fornaio to Pay $3 Million in EEOC Sexual Harassment Suit (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: Wagner Equipment to Pay $200,000 to Settle EEOC Disability and Retaliation Suit
description: The EEOC says the company required a 100-pound lift test that did not match the job and refused to let an employee return from medical leave.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The EEOC announced October 13, 2026 that Aurora, Colorado-based Wagner Equipment will pay $200,000 and provide other relief to settle a disability discrimination and retaliation lawsuit.

The EEOC alleged the company screened out an employee returning from medical leave by requiring a physical test of repeatedly lifting and carrying 100 pounds, although that did not reflect the essential functions of her job. It also alleged Wagner failed to reasonably accommodate her disability and retaliated by refusing to let her return to work in December 2021.

The two-year consent decree requires the company to review its accommodation policies and train employees and management in Colorado. The EEOC says the conduct violates the Americans with Disabilities Act. The case is EEOC v. Wagner Equipment Co., No. 1:26-cv-04802, in the District of Colorado.

sources.label: U.S. EEOC: Wagner Equipment to Pay $200,000 to Settle EEOC Disability and Retaliation Discrimination Suit (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: Michigan Regulators Share Tips to Avoid Scams During Medicare Open Enrollment
description: Open enrollment runs October 15 to December 7. Officials say never give your Medicare number to unsolicited callers and call 1-800-MEDICARE to verify.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Michigan’s Department of Insurance and Financial Services and Department of Health and Human Services warned older adults on October 12, 2026 about scams and high-pressure sales during Medicare Open Enrollment, October 15 through December 7, 2026.

Their tips: protect your Medicare ID number, which you only need to give when enrolling in a plan; do not share it with unsolicited callers, even if they claim to be Medicare, because CMS will never call or send someone to your home; do not trust caller ID, and hang up and call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227) to verify; ignore anyone who says you must join a Part D drug plan or lose coverage, since Part D is voluntary; and beware of mailings that look governmental but come from private companies.

Report scams to Michigan Senior Medicare Patrol at 844-677-6424, the Attorney General’s Consumer Protection Team at 517-335-7599, or DIFS at 877-999-6442. Free counseling is available from MI Options at 800-803-7174. The release also notes that the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan, which spreads drug costs into monthly payments, now renews automatically each year unless the enrollee opts out.

sources.label: Michigan DIFS: DIFS and MDHHS Share Tips to Help Older Adults Avoid Scams During Medicare Open Enrollment Period (Oct. 12, 2026)

title: Pennsylvania AG Charges Ex-Adjuster in $949,639 Fake Accident Claim Scheme
description: Prosecutors say Glenn Allen Johnson set up a sham law firm and used his insurer job to approve a payment to it.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday announced October 13, 2026 felony charges against Glenn Allen Johnson of Indiana and his business, Elite Injury Representatives, LLC, over a scheme to defraud Lancaster County-based Donegal Insurance of $949,639. The charges follow a presentment by the 55th Statewide Investigating Grand Jury and are allegations.

Investigators say Johnson was a Donegal claims adjuster in 2024 and 2025 when he created Elite Injury Representatives so it appeared to be a law firm, then entered fraudulent medical records and notes of conversations into an accident claim file. Based on that file and a demand letter believed to be written by Johnson, Donegal paid Elite $949,639.54.

He is charged with corrupt organizations, dealing in proceeds of unlawful activities, theft by deception, insurance fraud and forgery. He was arrested in Indiana last week and awaits extradition. Sunday said such fraud leads to higher premiums for law-abiding customers.

sources.label: Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General: AG Sunday’s Insurance Fraud Section Charges Man with Defrauding Lancaster County-Based Provider of Nearly $1M in Accident Claim Scheme (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: FTC and States Ask Court to Hold Martin Shkreli in Contempt of Industry Ban
description: The coalition alleges he traded and commented on pharma stocks in violation of a 2022 order that also required $64 million in disgorgement.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday announced October 13, 2026 that he joined the Federal Trade Commission and six other states in asking a federal judge to hold Martin Shkreli in contempt of a 2022 court order banning him from the pharmaceutical industry. The coalition alleges that since his release from prison in May 2022 he violated the order by publicly trading pharmaceutical stocks and broadcasting opinions about the business and management of pharma companies. These are allegations.

In February 2022 the Southern District of New York ruled Shkreli organized an illegal anticompetitive scheme to keep a monopoly over Daraprim, a treatment for toxoplasmosis, blocking generic competition and allowing the price to rise from $17.50 to $750 a tablet. The court imposed the industry ban and ordered him to disgorge over $64 million.
The motion and brief were filed October 13. The office said a court-ordered industry ban is a legal obligation, not a suggestion.

sources.label: Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General: Attorney General Sunday Seeks Contempt Finding Against Martin Shkreli for Allegedly Violating Lifetime Pharmaceutical Industry Ban (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: DOJ: Actions Against North Korean Remote IT Worker Schemes Affecting More Than 70 U.S. Companies
description: Prosecutors announced an indictment, two arrests and the seizure of about 187 computers from suspected laptop farms in Texas.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Justice Department announced October 13, 2026 coordinated actions against North Korean remote IT worker schemes that it says affected more than 70 U.S. companies. They include an indictment, two arrests, searches of multiple known or suspected “laptop farms” in Texas under “Operation Lonestar Roundup,” and the seizure of about 187 computer devices.

DOJ says North Korea uses remote IT work for U.S. companies to raise revenue for its regime. The department says the schemes threaten employers’ IT systems and data and leave many victims of identity theft, because workers use stolen identities. U.S. Attorney David Toepfer of the Northern District of Ohio urged U.S. companies to stay vigilant in their hiring practices.
The charges are allegations. Anyone hiring remote IT staff should verify identity and location carefully, as the actions show how stolen identities are used to get access inside American firms.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Justice: Justice Department Announces Coordinated Actions to Combat North Korean Remote IT Worker Schemes Affecting More than 70 U.S. Companies (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: SAVE Plan Borrowers Have 90 Days to Pick a New Repayment Plan, Federal Student Aid Says
description: Servicers began sending notices July 1, 2026. Borrowers who miss the final 30-day notice are placed in a fixed payment plan.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Federal Student Aid says a court order ended the SAVE Plan in March 2026, so borrowers enrolled in it must choose a different repayment plan. Borrowers who were never in SAVE, or who are in school, in a grace period, or hold a loan taken on or after July 1, 2026 that has not entered repayment, need to take no action.

Loan servicers started sending notices on July 1, 2026, in groups, so deadlines differ even within one servicer, and every SAVE borrower will be notified before the end of 2026. Each borrower has 90 days from the servicer notice. For a July 1 notice the deadline was September 29, 2026. Those who do not act get a final 30-day notice. The notice subject lines are “You Have 90 Days to Select a New Repayment Plan” and “Final Notice – You will be Placed into a New Repayment Plan in 30 Days.”

If no plan is chosen, the borrower is placed in the Standard Repayment Plan, or the Tiered Standard Plan if they hold a loan made on or after July 1, 2026 that is in repayment. Those payments may be higher than under an income-driven plan, and auto pay withdrawals rise with them. The servicer must give at least 21 days notice before the first due date on the new plan.
Federal Student Aid also notes that help from a federal loan servicer is free, and that borrowers never have to pay a company to apply for a repayment plan or manage federal loans.

sources.label: Federal Student Aid: SAVE Plan Borrowers: FAQs About Choosing a Different Repayment Plan

title: How Federal Student Loan Payments Are Calculated Under IBR, PAYE, RAP and Standard Plans
description: Federal Student Aid lists the payment formula and repayment period for each plan open to former SAVE borrowers.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: In its guidance for former SAVE Plan borrowers, Federal Student Aid lists how each plan sets the monthly payment. Income-Based Repayment is 15% of discretionary income (10% for new borrowers, whose first loan was made on or after July 1, 2014), never more than the 10-year Standard payment, over 25 years (20 for new borrowers). Pay As You Earn is 10% of discretionary income over 20 years. Income-Contingent Repayment is the lesser of 20% of discretionary income or a 12-year fixed payment adjusted for income, over 25 years. PAYE and ICR end no later than July 1, 2028.

The Repayment Assistance Plan is 1% to 10% of adjusted gross income divided by 12, reduced by $50 for each dependent claimed, with a $10 monthly minimum and a 30-year period. It is open to Direct Loans disbursed at any time. On-time RAP payers get an interest subsidy if payments do not cover accrued interest and may receive a matching principal payment.

For loans disbursed before July 1, 2026, fixed options are Standard, Graduated and Extended. The Tiered Standard Plan, for newer loans, runs 10 years for balances under $25,000, 15 under $50,000, 20 under $100,000 and 25 above $100,000. Parent PLUS loans are not eligible for IBR, ICR, PAYE or RAP on their own, and some loan types qualify only after consolidation.
Federal Student Aid warns that a lower payment over a longer period can mean more interest and a later discharge date, and it offers a Repayment Calculator for personal estimates.

sources.label: Federal Student Aid: SAVE Plan Borrowers: FAQs About Choosing a Different Repayment Plan

title: Can’t Afford Your Student Loan Payment? What Federal Student Aid Says About Deferment and Forbearance
description: The agency says to contact your servicer, but warns that interest can still accrue and discharge progress can be affected.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Federal Student Aid says borrowers leaving the SAVE Plan who cannot afford payments on a different plan can ask their servicer for a deferment or forbearance, which temporarily pauses or lowers payments.

It cautions that interest can still accrue during these periods, and that they can affect discharge options such as Public Service Loan Forgiveness and income-driven repayment discharge. Repeated missed payments bring more serious consequences over time, including negative credit effects.

Borrowers with a pending income-driven repayment application, or who are pursuing PSLF, should check the agency’s guidance before switching. The IDR application is submitted online at StudentAid.gov/idr after logging in, and servicer help is free.

sources.label: Federal Student Aid: SAVE Plan Borrowers: FAQs About Choosing a Different Repayment Plan

title: FTC Alert: Sextortion “Help” Services Charged Thousands and Did Not Deliver, Agency Alleges
description: The FTC’s consumer alert names Digital Forensics and lists free steps for victims, including the 48-hour Take It Down rule.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The FTC published a consumer alert October 13, 2026 about companies that offer paid fixes for sextortion, where someone threatens to share intimate images unless paid. It cites its lawsuit against Digital Forensics, the company behind sites including BlackmailHelpline.com, DigitalForensics.com, CyberBlackmail911.com and SecurityBreach911.com. The FTC alleges the company falsely promised to stop sextortion threats, prevent explicit material from spreading and report perpetrators to criminal authorities, charged customers thousands of dollars, and failed to deliver. These are allegations.

The FTC’s advice: ignore and block the blackmailer, do not pay or give access to devices or financial accounts, tell someone you trust, and report to local police and the FBI (fbi.gov, 1-800-225-5324). Cases involving a minor go to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children’s CyberTipline.

For images shared without permission, report them to the platform. Under the Take It Down Act, platforms must remove intimate images within 48 hours of a request, for free. If one does not, report to the FTC at TakeItDown.ftc.gov. Before paying any service, search its name with words like “scam” or “complaint.”

sources.label: FTC Consumer Advice: How to avoid deceptive sextortion assistance services and find real help (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: North Carolina AG Launches Fuel Check as State Gas Tax Is Suspended Through Nov. 30
description: Drivers can report stations that do not pass along the 41-cent-per-gallon savings at ncdoj.gov/ncfuelcheck or 1-877-5-NO-SCAM.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: North Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson announced October 13, 2026 that he sent letters to gas retailers and distributors saying state law requires them to pass along savings from the suspended 41-cent-per-gallon gas tax, and launched N.C. Fuel Check. Session Law 2026-62 suspends the state tax on gasoline and diesel through November 30, 2026, effective October 10.

Prices will not drop everywhere at once. Stations pay the tax when they receive a new delivery, and many are still selling fuel bought with the tax already paid, which the law accounts for. NCDOJ says prices should come down as stations get new deliveries, which for most should happen within about a week.

NCDOJ will review public gas price data for outliers, such as a station whose prices stay well above comparable stations nearby. Drivers can report stations at ncdoj.gov/ncfuelcheck or call 1-877-5-NO-SCAM. The office asks for the date and time of the visit, the fuel grade, a photo of the price sign and receipt, a detailed explanation, and prices at nearby stations.

sources.label: North Carolina Department of Justice: Attorney General Jeff Jackson Launches N.C. Fuel Check, Puts Gas Retailers on Notice to Pass Along Tax Savings to Drivers (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: Minnesota AG Tells Regulators Utility Affordability Means Paying Bills Without Sacrificing Health, Safety or Dignity
description: Keith Ellison spoke at the Public Utilities Commission’s first session in a statewide investigation of electric and gas affordability.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison addressed the Public Utilities Commission on October 13, 2026 at its first informational session in a statewide investigation into the affordability of rate-regulated electric and natural gas service. State law has his office represent residential and small-business customers of investor-owned utilities in PUC matters.

Ellison said residential customers, unlike businesses, cannot pass cost increases on to anyone, and if they cannot pay they may have service disconnected, and renters may lose their homes. He cited an RMI definition of affordability as whether households can pay for essential energy services without sacrificing health or safety, and added “without sacrificing dignity.”

He noted that gas bills from November to March are much higher than summer bills for Minnesotans, and that affordability means more than the per-kilowatt-hour rate or an average bill. His office’s consumer help line is 651-296-3353 in the Twin Cities and 800-657-3787 elsewhere in Minnesota.

sources.label: Minnesota Attorney General: ‘It’s hard to afford your life if you can’t afford your electric bill’ (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: IRS Tax Relief for Indiana Storm and Flood Victims: Deadlines Postponed to Feb. 1, 2027
description: The IRS news release was updated October 8 to add more counties. Late penalties in the postponement period can be abated by calling the notice number.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The IRS announced tax relief for Indiana individuals and businesses affected by severe storms, straight-line winds, tornadoes and flooding that began August 11, 2026. Affected taxpayers have until February 1, 2027 to file various returns and pay taxes originally due in that period. The release (IN-2026-01, dated September 2) was updated October 8, 2026 to add counties; taxpayers should check the IRS page for the current county list.

The relief does not cover 2025 income tax payments, which were due April 15, 2026. It covers estimated tax payments due on or after August 11, 2026, and quarterly payroll and certain excise returns normally due November 2, 2026. Payroll and excise deposit penalties are abated only if deposits were made by August 26, 2026.

The IRS applies relief automatically to taxpayers in the covered area. Those outside it, such as people whose records are in the area, can call 866-562-5227. Anyone who gets a late filing or payment penalty notice for a date in the postponement period should call the number on the notice to have it abated. Disaster casualty losses can be claimed on the return for the year of the event or the prior year.

sources.label: Internal Revenue Service: IRS announces tax relief for taxpayers impacted by severe storms, straight-line winds, tornadoes, and flooding in Indiana, various deadlines postponed to Feb. 1, 2027 (IN-2026-01, updated Oct. 8, 2026)

title: Michigan Unemployment Agency Warns: It Never Charges a Fee to Release Benefits
description: The UIA’s Cybersecurity Awareness Month tips cover fake calls, texts and emails, password hygiene and where to report unemployment fraud.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: Michigan’s Unemployment Insurance Agency said October 13, 2026 that it is promoting online safety during Cybersecurity Awareness Month. It warned that this summer a phone scam had callers falsely claiming unpaid unemployment benefits were available for a fee. The agency says it never charges a fee to release benefits and never contacts people to demand payment or personal information.

Its tips: be cautious of unsolicited calls, emails, texts or social media messages claiming to be from the UIA, and verify by logging in to your MiWAM or MiUI account; never share your Social Security number, login or bank details in response to random contacts; use a strong, unique password for MiWAM or MiLogin; review your account regularly and report unfamiliar activity; and log out fully on shared computers.

Unemployment fraud or identity theft can be reported at Michigan.gov/UIA. The agency also lists free help for claimants, including an Advocacy Program that provides free legal help for unemployed workers and employers who appeal UIA redeterminations, online coaching sessions on topics such as understanding a Monetary Determination letter and the protest and appeals process, and language assistance in Spanish, Arabic, Albanian, Bengali and Chinese.

sources.label: Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity: Unemployment agency promotes online safety during Cybersecurity Awareness Month (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: What to Do When a Debt Collector Contacts You, According to the CFPB
description: Collectors generally must give validation information within five days of first contact. Ignoring a valid debt usually will not make it go away.
author: Kseniya Dzigava
body: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau says a first contact from a debt collector is a chance to learn about the debt and whether it is yours. In general, the collector must give validation information during that first communication or within five days: the creditor’s name, the amount owed and how to dispute it. If the collector cannot or will not provide it, the CFPB says it could be a scam, and you should not give sensitive financial information to the caller until you confirm they are legitimate.
The agency also says that if the debt is valid, ignoring calls usually will not make the collector go away; they may look for other ways to collect, including a lawsuit.

The CFPB offers sample letters for saying you do not owe the debt, asking for more information, asking the collector to stop contacting you, asking them to contact you only through your lawyer, and specifying how they may contact you.
